Iteration 1/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: I registered broad, mechanistic, falsifiable associations for the first discovery pass. Because dependency scores are more negative when dependency is stronger, a negative exposed-minus-comparator mean difference is interpreted as stronger dependency, while a positive difference is interpreted as weaker dependency. The first group tests classical driver/pathway hypotheses: KRAS mutation with KRAS dependency, BRAF V600E with BRAF dependency, EGFR amplification with EGFR dependency, ERBB2 amplification with ERBB2 dependency, SMARCA4 loss with collateral SMARCA2 dependency, TP53 loss with weaker MDM2 and USP7 dependencies because these liabilities are expected to depend on a functional p53/MDM2 axis, KEAP1 loss with stronger NFE2L2 dependency through activated NRF2 signaling, and MSI-H with stronger WRN dependency. MYC amplification is used to probe transcription/translation dependency for DHX9, POLR2A, and RPL11. Additional exploratory predictors test proliferation/secretory signaling or pathway bypass ideas: higher media serum versus 5% for KIF18A mitotic dependency, PTEN loss for STAT3 dependency, ERBB2 amplification for TMED10 secretory dependency, and KRAS mutation for RIT1 dependency with the alternative prediction that downstream KRAS activation makes upstream RIT1 less essential. These are association hypotheses in this dataset only; causal interpretation or generalizability will require careful follow-up and validation. Initial statuses are unresolved because all effect sizes and uncertainty are yet to be estimated.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional

plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: The discovery set strongly supports three large associations in this dataset: SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency; MSI-H is associated with much stronger WRN dependency; and TP53 loss is associated with much weaker USP7 dependency. Each of these effects is far larger than a plausible 10% relative-difference benchmark and has very precise Welch intervals that exclude the null, so they are scientifically meaningful associations in the supplied data. I request validation for the surprising KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 association because the observed direction is opposite the prespecified hypothesis: the signed interval for H7 is robustly negative, meaning the raw contrast is positive and KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency by roughly 0.8 dependency-score units. Validation is useful because the magnitude is large and the direction reversal is consequential for follow-up claims. The KEAP1-loss hypothesis itself is rejected, but a reversed claim is registered as H17 for subsequent analysis. EGFR amplification is borderline: the point estimate is about 0.025, near the 10% threshold relative to overall dependency scale, but the 95% interval barely includes null, so it is kept active and a subgroup-specific analysis is registered. KRAS/BRAF/EGFR/ERBB2 driver and amplification effects for their matched targets, MYC-amplification associations with DHX9/POLR2A/RPL11, and TP53-loss associations with MDM2 are mostly small or imprecise. Several are rejected because the upper bound for the hypothesized clinically meaningful direction is below or essentially at the 10% threshold, and some are kept unresolved when intervals still span potentially meaningful positive effects. No causal interpretation is assigned; these are associations in the supplied dataset, and screen-quality or batch effects were not adjusted, although such confounding is unlikely to explain the very large H5, H8, and H12 effects.

record.narrative:
The new validation decisively resolves the surprising KEAP1-loss finding. For original H7, whose hypothesized direction was stronger NFE2L2 dependency, the independent validation estimate remains strongly negative after sign orientation (signed estimate -0.8005, 99.6%-adjusted interval approximately -0.829 to -0.772). Equivalently, the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is about +0.80 dependency-score units, meaning KEAP1-loss lines have substantially weaker NFE2L2 dependency rather than stronger dependency. This is far larger than the prespecified 10% relative-difference clinical-significance benchmark and is consistent across discovery and validation. Therefore the original directional hypothesis is rejected, but the reversed association, registered as H17, is accepted for this dataset. It should be interpreted as a reproducible dataset-specific association, not as proof of causal biology or external generalizability. It is surprising under simple KEAP1/NRF2 logic, so follow-up should examine subgroup robustness and whether it reflects redundancy, context-specific dependency, or a constructed data feature.

The other major accepted discovery findings remain scientifically compelling because their effects are enormous relative to dependency-scale and uncertainty is very small: SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-H is associated with much stronger WRN dependency, and TP53 loss is associated with much weaker USP7 dependency. These support the utility of broad CRISPR dependency mining for collateral lethality, MSI-associated WRN dependency, and p53-state dependence of USP7 dependency, though causal and therapeutic generalizability remain unresolved.

Negative or unsupported prespecified mechanistic claims include BRAF V600E-associated stronger BRAF dependency and MYC amplification-associated stronger dependencies on DHX9, POLR2A, and RPL11. In each, either the point estimate is small, the direction is not consistently supportive, or the interval does not provide evidence for a clinically meaningful effect in the hypothesized direction. EGFR amplification remains the most interesting borderline discovery result: the signed estimate is about 0.025 toward stronger EGFR dependency, close to the clinical-significance threshold relative to dependency scale, but the 95% interval barely includes the null. I will not accept H3 yet. The subgroup analysis in adenocarcinoma and the newly proposed KRAS and ERBB2 adenocarcinoma analyses are useful because driver dependencies can be context-dependent.

For the next analysis cycle, the most informative targets are: the still-untested exploratory predictors H13-H16, the EGFR adenocarcinoma subgroup H18, and the newly registered follow-ups: H19 checks robustness of the validated reversed KEAP1/NFE2L2 association; H20 asks whether other SWI/SNF lesions, specifically ARID1A loss, show SMARCA2 collateral-like dependency; H21 uses BRCA2 loss to probe specificity of WRN dependency beyond MSI-H; H22 and H23 test KRAS and ERBB2 dependencies in adenocarcinoma, where driver context is most expected. These will refine the map of which associations are stable, biologically coherent, or dataset-specific artifacts.

record.narrative:
I registered two classes of scientifically useful follow-up hypotheses. First, I tested context dependence in adenocarcinoma for the strongest current associations: SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, MSI-H/WRN, TP53-loss/USP7, and TP53-loss/MDM2. The first three are accepted or highly suggestive global dataset-specific effects, while the fourth probes a mechanistically related p53-MDM2 dependency that was weak in the global test. A negative raw contrast means stronger dependency; for USP7 and MDM2, the anticipated raw contrast is positive because TP53 loss was expected to weaken those dependencies. The alternative hypotheses are that the effects are not maintained in adenocarcinoma or are even reversed because lineage context changes pathway dependence.

Second, I added new mechanistic comparisons focused on pathway bypass, proliferation, and transcriptional dependence. BRAF V600E lies downstream of RIT1-RAS signaling, so I anticipated weaker RIT1 dependency in BRAF-mutant lines. KRAS mutation lies downstream of EGFR and ERBB2 receptor signaling, so I anticipated weaker EGFR and ERBB2 dependencies in KRAS-mutant lines if these cells bypass the receptor nodes. MYC amplification and RB1 loss both increase proliferative or cell-cycle transcriptional programs, so I predicted stronger KIF18A and POLR2A dependencies. PIK3CA mutation can activate AKT and related inflammatory-survival signaling, so I tested stronger STAT3 dependency. All alternatives include null effects, partial redundancy in signaling, or technical confounding by growth rate or screen state. These proposals expand the discovery map beyond driver-target matching while keeping the comparison cells large enough for Welch analysis.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous

throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: The new discovery batch strongly supports the previously accepted large associations in the dominant adenocarcinoma context: KEAP1 loss remains associated with substantially weaker NFE2L2 dependency, SMARCA4 loss with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-H with much stronger WRN dependency, and TP53 loss with much weaker USP7 dependency. These effects are far beyond any reasonable 10% relative-difference benchmark and have tight intervals excluding the null, so I accept them as dataset-specific associations while continuing to withhold causal or external-generalization claims. The most informative new discovery is H14: PTEN loss is associated with much stronger STAT3 dependency, with a signed estimate of about 0.27 and a very tight positive interval. This is a large, surprising, and potentially biologically meaningful association, so I accept it provisionally and request independent validation. Validation is warranted because PTEN loss may co-occur with other genomic or cell-state features, and this analysis is unadjusted; an independent check should reduce the chance that this is a local sample artifact, although it will still not establish mechanism. Many other tested hypotheses are null or too small: media serum 10 vs 5 does not meaningfully change KIF18A dependency; KRAS mutation does not meaningfully weaken RIT1 dependency; ARID1A loss does not show the SMARCA4-like collateral SMARCA2 effect; ERBB2 amplification in adenocarcinoma shows no meaningful stronger ERBB2 dependency and the point estimate is actually in the opposite direction. Some results remain unresolved because their intervals are compatible with null and small supportive effects: EGFR amplification in adenocarcinoma, KRAS mutation in adenocarcinoma, and BRCA2 loss as a WRN specificity probe. These are not rejected outright because the upper confidence bounds still allow borderline effects, but they do not currently support scientifically meaningful conclusions. I registered follow-ups to test whether the new PTEN-loss/STAT3 association is robust in adenocarcinoma and whether it persists when TP53 loss is excluded, because TP53 co-inheritance is a plausible competing explanation or modifier.

First, I tested context dependence in adenocarcinoma for the strongest current associations: SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, MSI-H/WRN, TP53-loss/USP7, and TP53-loss/MDM2. The first three are accepted or highly suggestive global dataset-specific effects, while the fourth probes a mechanistically related p53-MDM2 dependency that was weak in the global test. A negative raw contrast means stronger dependency; for USP7 and MDM2, the anticipated raw contrast is positive because TP53 loss was expected to weaken those dependencies. The alternative hypotheses are that the effects are not maintained in adenocarcinoma or are even reversed because lineage context changes pathway dependence.\n\nSecond, I added new mechanistic comparisons focused on pathway bypass, proliferation, and transcriptional dependence. BRAF V600E lies downstream of RIT1-RAS signaling, so I anticipated weaker RIT1 dependency in BRAF-mutant lines. KRAS mutation lies downstream of EGFR and ERBB2 receptor signaling, so I anticipated weaker EGFR and ERBB2 dependencies in KRAS-mutant lines if these cells bypass the receptor nodes. MYC amplification and RB1 loss both increase proliferative or cell-cycle transcriptional programs, so I predicted stronger KIF18A and POLR2A dependencies. record.narrative: The independent validation for H14 resolves the new PTEN-loss/STAT3-dependency discovery in favor of the hypothesized direction. The signed discovery estimate was about +0.267 (95% interval approximately +0.215 to +0.319), and because the hypothesis direction was -1, the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast was negative: PTEN-loss lines had lower dependency_STAT3 scores, meaning stronger STAT3 dependency. The independent validation estimate was about +0.310 with a very wide-adjusted but still strongly positive interval approximately +0.231 to +0.388. This is larger than the prespecified 10% relative-difference benchmark on the dependency-score scale and is not compatible with a null effect. Therefore H14 is accepted for this dataset: PTEN loss is associated with substantially stronger STAT3 dependency. This should still be interpreted as an association in the supplied cell lines, not as proof that PTEN loss causes STAT3 dependency or that the relationship generalizes outside this dataset. I registered two interaction follow-ups because they directly test whether the PTEN-loss effect is modified by lineage subtype or TP53-loss state, which is more informative than separate subgroup estimates alone. Overall, the strongest supported dataset-specific findings remain: SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-H is associated with much stronger WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency after the prespecified hypothesis was reversed, and TP53 loss is associated with much weaker USP7 dependency. The PTEN-loss/STAT3 result is now the newest accepted large effect, with independent internal validation. Negative or unsupported results include BRAF V600E-associated stronger BRAF dependency, MYC amplification-associated stronger dependencies on DHX9/POLR2A/RPL11, media-serum effects on KIF18A, KRAS mutation-associated weaker RIT1 dependency, ARID1A-loss-associated stronger SMARCA2 dependency, and ERBB2 amplification-associated stronger ERBB2 dependency in adenocarcinoma. Several driver-amplification or driver-mutation effects remain unresolved but not accepted because their estimates are small or intervals span null, including EGFR amplification, KRAS mutation effects on KRAS dependency, and ERBB2 amplification globally. The next best use of analysis capacity is to complete the untested mechanistic bypass and proliferation hypotheses H15 and H27-H33, examine PTEN/STAT3 context dependence through H34-H35 and the two new interactions, and then reserve validation for any new large or surprising effect that cannot be resolved by robustness checks.

  "narrative": "I registered three complementary sets of hypotheses. First, I focused on the newly accepted PTEN-loss/STAT3-dependency association because it is one of the few large noncanonical associations and may be modified by other PI3K/MAPK pathway lesions. The PTEN-loss-by-PIK3CA-mutation interaction tests whether PTEN loss and PIK3CA mutation are synergistic, redundant, or independent with respect to STAT3 dependency. The PTEN-loss-by-KRAS-mutation interaction tests whether KRAS-driven signaling either reinforces STAT3 dependency through oncogenic stress or attenuates PTEN-loss effects through pathway redundancy. A separate PIK3CA-mutation test restricted to PTEN-wild-type lines tests whether PI3K activation is sufficient for stronger STAT3 dependency when PTEN status is not confounding the comparison. Second, I probed the surprising accepted reversed KEAP1/NFE2L2 finding, where KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency. STK11 loss is a plausible co-mutational context in lung adenocarcinoma, so I registered an interaction test, a main effect test for STK11 loss, and a robustness test of the KEAP1-loss effect in STK11-wild-type lines. record.narrative: I registered targeted context and robustness analyses around the strongest dataset-specific associations rather than continuing broadly with lower-yield bypass probes. For the newly validated PTEN-loss/STAT3 result, I added two interaction tests to ask whether the effect is synergistic, redundant, or independent in the presence of PIK3CA mutation or KRAS mutation. I also registered a PIK3CA-mutation test restricted to PTEN-wild-type lines to ask whether PI3K activation is sufficient for stronger STAT3 dependency when PTEN status is not part of the comparison. For the accepted reversed KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 finding, I added an STK11-loss interaction and a KEAP1-loss effect in STK11-wild-type lines to test whether the large association is genuinely KEAP1-specific or is carried by co-occurring STK11 loss, a common co-mutational context in lung adenocarcinoma. I also registered robustness checks that remove plausible co-mutational confounders for the largest accepted effects: SMARCA4 loss restricted to TP53-wild-type lines, MSI-H/WRN restricted to TP53-wild-type lines, and EGFR amplification restricted to KRAS-wild-type lines. These tests distinguish stable dataset associations from effects diluted or induced by common alternative driver states. I deferred several lower-priority active hypotheses, including broad bypass and proliferation probes, because the current analysis budget is best spent resolving the strongest accepted effects and their context dependence. These proposals remain association-level analyses in the supplied dataset and are not causal or generalizability claims.

interaction with STK11 loss and KEAP1 effect in STK11-wt, SMARCA4-SMARCA2 in TP53-wt, MSI-WRN in TP53-wt, and EGFR amplification in KRAS-wt. Accepted dataset-specific associations: SMARCA4 loss -> stronger SMARCA2 dependency; MSI-H -> stronger WRN dependency; KEAP1 loss -> weaker NFE2L2 dependency; TP53 loss -> weaker USP7 dependency; PTEN loss -> stronger STAT3 dependency. Future validation should be reserved for a newly discovered large surprising association or a decisive context interaction that changes interpretation. Lower-priority deferred hypotheses include TMED10/ERBB2, MDM2/TP53 adenocarcinoma, RIT1/BRAF bypass, EGFR/ERBB2/KRAS bypass, MYC/KIF18A, RB1/POLR2A, and PIK3CA/STAT3 global effect.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"I registered targeted context and robustness analyses around the strongest dataset-specific associations rather than continuing broadly with lower-yield bypass probes. For the newly validated PTEN-loss/STAT3 result, I added two interaction tests to ask whether the effect is synergistic, redundant, or independent in the presence of PIK3CA mutation or KRAS mutation. I also registered a PIK3CA-mutation test restricted to PTEN-wild-type lines to ask whether PI3K activation is sufficient for stronger STAT3 dependency when PTEN status is not part of the comparison. For the accepted reversed KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 finding, I added an STK11-loss interaction and a KEAP1-loss effect in STK11-wild-type lines to test whether the large association is genuinely KEAP1-specific or is carried by co-occurring STK11 loss, a common co-mutational context in lung adenocarcinoma. I also registered robustness checks that remove plausible co-mutational confounders for the largest accepted effects: SMARCA4 loss restricted to TP53-wild-type lines, MSI-H/WRN restricted to TP53-wild-type lines, and EGFR amplification restricted to KRAS-wild-type lines. These tests distinguish stable dataset associations from effects diluted or induced by common alternative driver states. I deferred several lower-priority active hypotheses, including broad bypass and proliferation probes, because the current analysis budget is best spent resolving the strongest accepted effects and their context dependence. These proposals remain association-level analyses in the supplied dataset and are not causal or generalizability claims.","analyze":"I selected 12 untested active comparisons that either complete the original broad discovery pass or test the most informative follow-up claims. H13, H14, and H16 probe media-serum effects on KIF18A, PTEN-loss effects on STAT3, and KRAS-mutation effects on RIT1 dependency, respectively. H18 tests the borderline EGFR-amplification signal in adenocarcinoma, where receptor-driven context is more plausible. H19, H24, H25, and H26 test whether the strongest accepted dataset-specific associations are retained in adenocarcinoma: KEAP1-loss/weak NFE2L2, SMARCA4-loss/strong SMARCA2, MSI-H/strong WRN, and TP53-loss/weak USP7. H20 and H21 test specificity or related collateral-dependency mechanisms: ARID1A loss for SMARCA2 and BRCA2 loss for WRN. H22 and H23 revisit KRAS and ERBB2 amplification dependencies in adenocarcinoma, where driver context may matter. I deferred H15 and H27 because they are exploratory or less central, and H28-H33 for later if capacity remains.","appraise":"The new discovery batch strongly supports the previously accepted large associations in the dominant adenocarcinoma context: KEAP1 loss remains associated with substantially weaker NFE2L2 dependency, SMARCA4 loss with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-H with much stronger WRN dependency, and TP53 loss with much weaker USP7 dependency. These effects are far beyond any reasonable 10% relative-difference benchmark and have tight intervals excluding the null, so I accept them as dataset-specific associations while continuing to withhold causal or external-generalization claims. The most informative new discovery is H14: PTEN loss is associated with much stronger STAT3 dependency, with a signed estimate of about 0.27 and a very tight positive interval. This is a large, surprising, and potentially biologically meaningful association, so I accept it provisionally and request independent validation. Validation is warranted because PTEN loss may co-occur with other genomic or cell-state features, and this analysis is unadjusted; an independent check should reduce the chance that this is a local sample artifact, although it will still not establish mechanism. Many other tested hypotheses are null or too small: media serum 10 vs 5 does not meaningfully change KIF18A dependency; KRAS mutation does not meaningfully weaken RIT1 dependency; ARID1A loss does not show the SMARCA4-like collateral SMARCA2 effect; ERBB2 amplification in adenocarcinoma shows no meaningful stronger ERBB2 dependency and the point estimate is actually in the opposite direction. Some results remain unresolved because their intervals are compatible with null and small supportive effects: EGFR amplification in adenocarcinoma, KRAS mutation in adenocarcinoma, and BRCA2 loss as a WRN specificity probe. These are not rejected outright because the upper confidence bounds still allow borderline effects, but they do not currently support scientifically meaningful conclusions. I registered follow-ups to test whether the new PTEN-loss/STAT3 association is robust in adenocarcinoma and whether it persists when TP53 loss is excluded, because TP53 co-inheritance is a plausible competing explanation or modifier.","synthesize":"The independent validation for H14 resolves the new PTEN-loss/STAT3-dependency discovery in favor of the hypothesized direction. The signed discovery estimate was about +0.267 (95% interval approximately +0.215 to +0.319), and because the hypothesis direction was -1, the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast was negative: PTEN-loss lines had lower dependency_STAT3 scores, meaning stronger STAT3 dependency. The independent validation estimate was about +0.310 with a very wide-adjusted but still strongly positive interval approximately +0.231 to +0.388. This is larger than the prespecified 10% relative-difference benchmark on the dependency-score scale and is not compatible with a null effect. Therefore H14 is accepted for this dataset: PTEN loss is associated with substantially stronger STAT3 dependency. This should still be interpreted as an association in the supplied cell lines, not as proof that PTEN loss causes STAT3 dependency or that the relationship generalizes outside this dataset. I registered two interaction follow-ups because they directly test whether the PTEN-loss effect is modified by lineage subtype or TP53-loss state, which is more informative than separate subgroup estimates alone. Overall, the strongest supported dataset-specific findings remain: SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-H is associated with much stronger WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency after the prespecified hypothesis was reversed, and TP53 loss is associated with much weaker USP7 dependency. The PTEN-loss/STAT3 result is now the newest accepted large effect, with independent internal validation. record.narrative: These twelve follow-up analyses mostly confirm that the already accepted large associations are robust to common co-mutational contexts, rather than revealing new large effects. For PTEN loss and STAT3 dependency, H34 and H35 show that the association is essentially unchanged in adenocarcinoma and remains robust when TP53-loss lines are excluded: both signed estimates are roughly +0.27 to +0.29 with intervals far from zero and far beyond the 10% difference benchmark. The raw interpretation remains that PTEN-loss lines have more negative STAT3 dependency scores, i.e. stronger STAT3 dependency. This is not a new causal claim, but it materially strengthens the dataset-specific evidence for the accepted PTEN-loss association. H36 found no evidence that lineage subtype modifies the PTEN-loss effect; the interaction point estimate is near zero, but the interval is wide enough that a moderate interaction cannot be excluded, so I leave it unresolved and deferred rather than claiming absence. H37 was the only interaction test with a nontrivial point estimate, but it is in the direction opposite to the hypothesized negative interaction: the signed estimate is negative, implying PTEN loss may be less strongly associated with STAT3 dependency in TP53-loss lines. Because the interval is wide and the exposed PTEN-loss/TP53-loss cell is small, I do not accept it as decisive; I reject the original hypothesized direction and close it without validation because it does not overturn the main PTEN-loss finding and is not strong enough to justify spending an independent validation. H38 and H39 showed no evidence of PIK3CA- or KRAS-mutation modification of the PTEN-loss STAT3 association; intervals are broad and centered near zero, so I record them as unresolved but deferred, not as evidence for meaningful context dependence. H40 rejects PIK3CA mutation as a driver of stronger STAT3 dependency among PTEN-wild-type lines: the effect is tiny and the interval excludes meaningful magnitude. For the reversed KEAP1/NFE2L2 association, H41 shows no meaningful modification by STK11-loss status, and H42 shows that the large KEAP1-loss association is essentially intact in STK11-wild-type lines. This makes it unlikely that the accepted KEAP1/NFE2L2 result is carried by STK11-loss co-occurrence. H43 and H44 likewise show that the very large SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 and MSI-high/WRN associations persist in TP53-wild-type lines with nearly unchanged huge effects. These are strong dataset-specific robustness results, not causal or external-generalization claims.   "narrative": "The newly released validation evidence resolves the two due claims decisively. Therefore I keep H7 rejected and closed, and I keep the reversed claim H17 accepted: KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency. Validation strengthens the dataset-specific conclusion but does not by itself establish mechanism, causality, or broad applicability beyond these cell lines.\n\nThe current supported set now includes five validated large dataset-specific associations: SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency (after reversal), PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, plus the accepted reversed KEAP1/NFE2L2 result. record.narrative:
The newly released validation evidence resolves the two due claims decisively. For H5, the discovery result linked SMARCA4 loss to much stronger SMARCA2 dependency (signed estimate about +0.784, raw contrast negative because the hypothesis direction was -1), and the independent validation estimate was about +0.799 with interval approximately +0.768 to +0.832. This is enormously larger than the 10% practical difference benchmark and has an interval far from zero. H5 therefore remains accepted as a very strong dataset-specific association: SMARCA4-loss lines have more negative SMARCA2 dependency scores, meaning stronger dependency. This remains an association in the supplied lung cell-line dataset, not causal evidence or a claim of external generalizability.

For H7, the original hypothesis was that KEAP1 loss would be associated with stronger NFE2L2 dependency. The discovery evidence already contradicted that direction, and the new validation independently confirms it: signed estimate about -0.8005 with interval approximately -0.829 to -0.772 under direction -1. That corresponds to a raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast of roughly +0.80, meaning KEAP1-loss lines have higher NFE2L2 dependency scores, i.e. weaker NFE2L2 dependency. Therefore I keep H7 rejected and closed, and I keep the reversed claim H17 accepted: KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency. Validation strengthens the dataset-specific conclusion but does not by itself establish mechanism, causality, or broad applicability beyond these cell lines.

The current supported set now includes five validated large dataset-specific associations: SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency (after reversal), PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, plus the accepted reversed KEAP1/NFE2L2 result. Additional accepted large effects remain MSI-H with stronger WRN dependency and TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency, supported by robust subgroup and co-mutational restrictions even though not yet independently validated. Other robustness analyses showed that the major accepted effects are not explained by adenocarcinoma restriction, TP53 loss, STK11 loss, or KRAS-wild-type restriction. The strongest negative findings include BRAF V600E not showing stronger BRAF dependency, MYC amplification not increasing dependencies on DHX9/POLR2A/RPL11, media serum effects on KIF18A being negligible, KRAS mutation not causing weaker RIT1 dependency, ARID1A loss not mimicking SMARCA4 loss for SMARCA2, and ERBB2 amplification not showing meaningful ERBB2 dependency in adenocarcinoma. Many other driver or pathway probes remain unresolved because their intervals include null and their point estimates are too small to support meaningful conclusions.

For the next analysis round, I am activating the untested mechanistic bypass and proliferation probes H15 and H28-H33, and adding five new pathway-specificity hypotheses. The new STAT3 driver tests ask whether ERBB2 amplification, EGFR amplification, KRAS mutation, or PIK3CA mutation are associated with stronger STAT3 dependency; this directly tests whether the accepted PTEN-loss effect is one node among several pathway associations or a more selective STAT3 signal. The NF1-loss test asks whether RAS-pathway disruption is associated with stronger KRAS dependency, a biologically meaningful alternative to KRAS mutation itself. The PTEN-loss test on EGFR dependency asks whether the PTEN-loss effect extends to RTK dependencies or remains specific to STAT3 after the earlier STAT3 and EGFR/KRAS bypass probes are considered. This next batch is the most informative because it continues broad exploration while remaining anchored to the strongest accepted findings and the 10% difference threshold.

I also registered a PIK3CA-mutation test restricted to PTEN-wild-type lines to ask whether PI3K activation is sufficient for stronger STAT3 dependency when PTEN status is not part of the comparison. For the accepted reversed KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 finding, I added an STK11-loss interaction and a KEAP1-loss effect in STK11-wild-type lines to test whether the large association is genuinely KEAP1-specific or is carried by co-occurring STK11 loss, a common co-mutational context in lung adenocarcinoma. I also registered robustness checks that remove plausible co-mutational confounders for the largest accepted effects: SMARCA4 loss restricted to TP53-wild-type lines, MSI-H/WRN restricted to TP53-wild-type lines, and EGFR amplification restricted to KRAS-wild-type lines. These tests distinguish stable dataset associations from effects diluted or induced by common alternative driver states. These proposals remain association-level analyses in the supplied dataset and are not causal or generalizability claims.","analyze":"I selected the twelve highest-priority active follow-up analyses because they directly test robustness and context dependence of the strongest accepted dataset associations rather than pursuing lower-yield mechanistic bypass probes. H34-H37 characterize the newly accepted PTEN-loss/STAT3 association: its adenocarcinoma subgroup, its persistence after excluding TP53-loss lines, and whether the contrast is modified by lineage subtype or TP53-loss state. H38-H39 add interaction tests for whether PTEN loss interacts with PIK3CA mutation or KRAS mutation, two plausible pathway-redundancy contexts that could alter STAT3 dependence. H40 asks whether PIK3CA mutation is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency when PTEN status is fixed at wild-type, separating PI3K-pathway activation from PTEN-loss co-occurrence. H41-H42 test the large reversed KEAP1-loss/weak NFE2L2 result against STK11-loss context, a common co-mutational state in lung adenocarcinoma, and ask whether KEAP1 loss remains important in STK11-wild-type lines. H43 and H44 retest the largest collateral dependencies, SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 and MSI-high/WRN, in TP53-wild-type lines to ask whether these effects are robust to TP53 co-mutation structure. H45 tests EGFR amplification restricted to KRAS-wild-type lines, addressing whether a weak KRAS co-occurrence signal was diluting the EGFR-amplification effect. This batch is therefore concentrated on whether accepted associations are specific, reproducible under common co-mutational restrictions, and meaningfully modified by biological context.","appraise":"These twelve follow-up analyses mostly confirm that the already accepted large associations are robust to common co-mutational contexts, rather than revealing new large effects. For PTEN loss and STAT3 dependency, H34 and H35 show that the association is essentially unchanged in adenocarcinoma and remains robust when TP53-loss lines are excluded: both signed estimates are roughly +0.27 to +0.29 with intervals far from zero and far beyond the 10% difference benchmark. The raw interpretation remains that PTEN-loss lines have more negative STAT3 dependency scores, i.e. stronger STAT3 dependency. This is not a new causal claim, but it materially strengthens the dataset-specific evidence for the accepted PTEN-loss association. H36 found no evidence that lineage subtype modifies the PTEN-loss effect; the interaction point estimate is near zero, but the interval is wide enough that a moderate interaction cannot be excluded, so I leave it unresolved and deferred rather than claiming absence. H37 was the only interaction test with a nontrivial point estimate, but it is in the direction opposite to the hypothesized negative interaction: the signed estimate is negative, implying PTEN loss may be less strongly associated with STAT3 dependency in TP53-loss lines. Because the interval is wide and the exposed PTEN-loss/TP53-loss cell is small, I do not accept it as decisive; I reject the original hypothesized direction and close it without validation because it does not overturn the main PTEN-loss finding and is not strong enough to justify spending an independent validation. record.narrative: I registered a compact high-priority follow-up batch rather than continuing broadly with lower-yield bypass probes. The batch has three scientific purposes. First, it adds biologically plausible new predictor-outcome hypotheses that could represent additional large dataset-specific associations: MYC amplification may increase USP7 dependency because USP7 supports MYC/MDM2 network stability; CDKN2A loss may increase KIF18A dependency because unchecked cell-cycle entry can create mitotic requirements; and STK11 loss may be associated with STAT3 dependency in inflammatory or metabolic tumor contexts. These are all association hypotheses in the supplied lung cell-line dataset, not causal claims. Second, it tests robustness of two currently accepted but not yet independently validated large effects, MSI-H/WRN and TP53-loss/USP7, within high-quality CRISPR screens defined by screen_roc_auc at or above the dataset median. If these effects persist in high-quality screens, the evidence that they are not primarily screen-quality artifacts is strengthened; if they disappear, the accepted claims would need to be reconsidered. Third, it refines the largest accepted associations by testing plausible co-mutational modifiers: ARID1A loss as a chromatin-complex co-alteration for SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 dependency, TP53 loss for KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 dependency, MYC amplification for TP53-loss/USP7 dependency, and KEAP1 loss for PTEN-loss/STAT3 dependency. I also added a PTEN-loss/ERBB2 specificity probe next to the existing PTEN-loss/EGFR probe to determine whether PTEN loss is associated with broader RTK dependencies or remains relatively selective for STAT3. These proposals are prioritized because they either could reveal new meaningful effects or directly sharpen the biological and technical interpretation of the strongest currently supported findings.

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction

Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

These are all association hypotheses in the supplied lung cell-line dataset, not causal claims. If these effects persist in high-quality screens, the evidence that they are not primarily screen-quality artifacts is strengthened; if they disappear, the accepted claims would need to be reconsidered. Third, it refines the largest accepted associations by testing plausible co-mutational modifiers: ARID1A loss as a chromatin-complex co-alteration for SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 dependency, TP53 loss for KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 dependency, MYC amplification for TP53-loss/USP7 dependency, and KEAP1 loss for PTEN-loss/STAT3 dependency. This is not a new causal claim, but it materially strengthens the dataset-specific evidence for the accepted PTEN-loss association. H36 found no evidence that lineage subtype modifies the PTEN-loss effect; the interaction point estimate is near zero, but the interval is wide enough that a moderate interaction cannot be excluded, so I leave it unresolved and deferred rather than claiming absence. H37 was the only interaction test with a nontrivial point estimate, but it is in the direction opposite to the hypothesized negative interaction: the signed estimate is negative, implying PTEN loss may be less strongly associated with STAT3 dependency in TP53-loss lines. Because the interval is wide and the exposed PTEN-loss/TP53-loss cell is small, I do not accept it as decisive; I reject the original hypothesized direction and close it without validation because it does not overturn the main PTEN-loss finding and is not strong enough to justify spending an independent validation. H38 and H39 showed no evidence of PIK3CA- or KRAS-mutation modification of the PTEN-loss STAT3 association; intervals are broad and centered near zero, so I record them as unresolved but deferred, not as evidence for meaningful context dependence. H40 rejects PIK3CA mutation as a driver of stronger STAT3 dependency among PTEN-wild-type lines: the effect is tiny and the interval excludes meaningful magnitude. For the reversed KEAP1/NFE2L2 association, H41 shows no meaningful modification by STK11-loss status, and H42 shows that the large KEAP1-loss association is essentially intact in STK11-wild-type lines. This makes it unlikely that the accepted KEAP1/NFE2L2 result is carried by STK11-loss co-occurrence. H43 and H44 likewise show that the very large SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 and MSI-high/WRN associations persist in TP53-wild-type lines with nearly unchanged huge effects. These are strong dataset-specific robustness results, not causal or external-generalization claims. H45 found only a very small EGFR-amplification association in KRAS-wild-type lines, with an interval entirely below any meaningful 10% effect range and compatible with the null; this closes the idea that KRAS co-occurrence was masking a scientifically meaningful EGFR-amplification effect. This is enormously larger than the 10% practical difference benchmark and has an interval far from zero. H5 therefore remains accepted as a very strong dataset-specific association: SMARCA4-loss lines have more negative SMARCA2 dependency scores, meaning stronger dependency. This remains an association in the supplied lung cell-line dataset, not causal evidence or a claim of external generalizability.\n\nFor H7, the original hypothesis was that KEAP1 loss would be associated with stronger NFE2L2 dependency. The discovery evidence already contradicted that direction, and the new validation independently confirms it: signed estimate about -0.8005 with interval approximately -0.829 to -0.772 under direction -1. That corresponds to a raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast of roughly +0.80, meaning KEAP1-loss lines have higher NFE2L2 dependency scores, i.e. weaker NFE2L2 dependency. Therefore I keep H7 rejected and closed, and I keep the reversed claim H17 accepted: KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency. Validation strengthens the dataset-specific conclusion but does not by itself establish mechanism, causality, or broad applicability beyond these cell lines.\n\nThe current supported set now includes five validated large dataset-specific associations: SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency (after reversal), PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, plus the accepted reversed KEAP1/NFE2L2 result. Additional accepted large effects remain MSI-H with stronger WRN dependency and TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency, supported by robust subgroup and co-mutational restrictions even though not yet independently validated. Other robustness analyses showed that the major accepted effects are not explained by adenocarcinoma restriction, TP53 loss, STK11 loss, or KRAS-wild-type restriction. The strongest negative findings include BRAF V600E not showing stronger BRAF dependency, MYC amplification not increasing dependencies on DHX9/POLR2A/RPL11, media serum effects on KIF18A being negligible, KRAS mutation not causing weaker RIT1 dependency, ARID1A loss not mimicking SMARCA4 loss for SMARCA2, and ERBB2 amplification not showing meaningful ERBB2 dependency in adenocarcinoma. Many other driver or pathway probes remain unresolved because their intervals include null and their point estimates are too small to support meaningful conclusions.\n\nFor the next analysis round, I am activating the untested mechanistic bypass and proliferation probes H15 and H28-H33, and adding five new pathway-specificity hypotheses. The new STAT3 driver tests ask whether ERBB2 amplification, EGFR amplification, KRAS mutation, or PIK3CA mutation are associated with stronger STAT3 dependency; this directly tests whether the accepted PTEN-loss effect is one node among several pathway associations or a more selective STAT3 signal. The NF1-loss test asks whether RAS-pathway disruption is associated with stronger KRAS dependency, a biologically meaningful alternative to KRAS mutation itself. The PTEN-loss test on EGFR dependency asks whether the PTEN-loss effect extends to RTK dependencies or remains specific to STAT3 after the earlier STAT3 and EGFR/KRAS bypass probes are considered. This next batch is the most informative because it continues broad exploration while remaining anchored to the strongest accepted findings and the 10% difference threshold."}}

record.narrative: This batch separates strong robustness evidence from several near-null follow-ups. The two screen-quality robustness tests are convincing. H54 shows that MSI-high association with WRN dependency is essentially unchanged among lines with screen_roc_auc at or above the median: signed estimate about +0.790 with interval about +0.751 to +0.829. Under direction -1, this means MSI-high lines have substantially more negative WRN scores, i.e. much stronger WRN dependency, even in higher-quality screens. H55 similarly preserves the TP53-loss/USP7 association in high-quality screens, signed estimate about +0.426 with interval about +0.332 to +0.519; direction +1 means TP53-loss lines have higher USP7 scores, i.e. weaker USP7 dependency. Both are far from zero and large relative to the scale of the dependency scores, so multiplicity and ordinary sampling noise are not plausible explanations for these specific results. The remaining main-effect tests were biologically plausible but not supported: NF1 loss was not associated with stronger KRAS dependency (H49), PTEN loss was not associated with stronger EGFR dependency (H50), MYC amplification was not associated with stronger USP7 dependency (H51), CDKN2A loss was not associated with stronger KIF18A dependency (H52), and STK11 loss was not associated with stronger STAT3 dependency (H53). H60 further shows PTEN loss was not associated with stronger ERBB2 dependency. record.narrative: The newly delivered validation evidence supports the two due claims decisively. For H14, PTEN loss versus PTEN wild-type was tested with hypothesis direction -1, so a positive signed estimate corresponds to a raw negative exposed-minus-comparator contrast, meaning PTEN-loss lines have lower, i.e. more negative, STAT3 dependency scores and therefore stronger STAT3 dependency. Discovery gave a signed estimate about +0.267 with interval +0.215 to +0.319, and independent validation gave about +0.310 with interval +0.231 to +0.388. The validation interval is adjusted for the validation burden and remains far from zero. The magnitude is very large relative to the observed STAT3 score scale and standard deviation, so it far exceeds the practical 10% difference benchmark. I therefore keep H14 accepted and closed, as a dataset-specific association, not a causal or external-generalizability claim. For H8, MSI-high versus non-MSI-high also used direction -1, so signed positive estimates mean raw negative contrasts: MSI-high lines have much more negative WRN scores, i.e. stronger WRN dependency. Discovery signed estimate was about +0.790 with interval +0.760 to +0.819, and independent validation was about +0.807 with interval +0.759 to +0.855. The exposed MSI-high cell is small, but the validation effect remains enormous and precise enough that random noise or the small exposed group is not a plausible explanation. This is further supported by consistency with the high-quality-screen subset and other restrictions noted in related claims. I therefore keep H8 accepted and closed. With H8 now validated, the accepted large dataset-specific associations are SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency after reversal, PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, and MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency. The TP53-loss/USP7 association remains large and robust in the supplied dataset, including in high screen_roc_auc screens and adenocarcinoma subset, but has not yet had its own independent validation; I therefore mark H12 active as the next validation priority while leaving it accepted on existing evidence. The many negative closed probes remain informative but should not be overinterpreted as exact biological nulls; they simply fail to meet the practical-meaningfulness threshold in this dataset. Next analyses should focus on technical and co-mutational specificity of the largest accepted effects rather than chasing near-null interactions. I registered high-screen-quality robustness tests for SMARCA4/SMARCA2, KEAP1/NFE2L2, and PTEN/STAT3, plus co-alteration-restricted main-effect tests to test whether the main associations persist outside common confounding contexts. These are association tests in the supplied lung cell-line dataset only.

record.narrative: I registered a new round of context-specific refinements of the five largest supported dataset-specific associations, plus one mechanistically plausible new MDM2 probe. The central rationale is that the accepted effects are very large, so the most informative next question is not whether tiny additional main-effect probes are near zero, but whether the effects persist when co-altered genomic contexts and technical screen contexts differ. The proposed co-alteration main-effect tests examine SMARCA4 loss in ARID1A-loss and TP53-loss backgrounds, KEAP1 loss in TP53-loss background, PTEN loss in TP53-loss background, and TP53 loss in PTEN-wild-type background. These are complementary to prior interaction and co-restriction tests: interaction estimates are often imprecise and centered near zero, whereas direct conditional main effects tell whether the accepted contrast remains large inside a specific co-alteration stratum. The screen_roc_auc low/median robustness tests are not intended as causal claims about screen quality; they ask whether the associations are confined to apparently better screens. The CRISPR-Ky library tests ask whether the major associations are visible in a non-Avana technical setting. The new MYC-amplification/MDM2 test is restricted to TP53-wild-type cells because the MYC-MDM2-p53 axis is mechanistically most plausible there: MYC activation may create stronger MDM2 dependency when p53 signaling remains intact. This is a dataset-specific association hypothesis only, not a claim of causality or generalizability. These proposals are prioritized over near-null broad exploration because they either can establish important specificity of already strong effects or test a biologically focused new hypothesis with a clear p53-context rationale.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The proposed co-alteration main-effect tests examine SMARCA4 loss in ARID1A-loss and TP53-loss backgrounds, KEAP1 loss in TP53-loss background, PTEN loss in TP53-loss background, and TP53 loss in PTEN-wild-type background. The CRISPR-Ky library tests ask whether the major associations are visible in a non-Avana technical setting. The new MYC-amplification/MDM2 test is restricted to TP53-wild-type cells because the MYC-MDM2-p53 axis is mechanistically most plausible there: MYC activation may create stronger MDM2 dependency when p53 signaling remains intact. comparison cell.

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
