All results are to be interpreted as associations in the supplied lung cell-line dataset only.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"I registered a new round of context-specific refinements of the five largest supported dataset-specific associations, plus one mechanistically plausible new MDM2 probe. The central rationale is that the accepted effects are very large, so the most informative next question is not whether tiny additional main-effect probes are near zero, but whether the effects persist when co-altered genomic contexts and technical screen contexts differ. The proposed co-alteration main-effect tests examine SMARCA4 loss in ARID1A-loss and TP53-loss backgrounds, KEAP1 loss in TP53-loss background, PTEN loss in TP53-loss background, and TP53 loss in PTEN-wild-type background. These are complementary to prior interaction and co-restriction tests: interaction estimates are often imprecise and centered near zero, whereas direct conditional main effects tell whether the accepted contrast remains large inside a specific co-alteration stratum. The screen_roc_auc low/median robustness tests are not intended as causal claims about screen quality; they ask whether the associations are confined to apparently better screens. The CRISPR-Ky library tests ask whether the major associations are visible in a non-Avana technical setting. The new MYC-amplification/MDM2 test is restricted to TP53-wild-type cells because the MYC-MDM2-p53 axis is mechanistically most plausible there: MYC activation may create stronger MDM2 dependency when p53 signaling remains intact. This is a dataset-specific association hypothesis only, not a claim of causality or generalizability. These proposals are prioritized over near-null broad exploration because they either can establish important specificity of already strong effects or test a biologically focused new hypothesis with a clear p53-context rationale.","analyze":"I selected 12 currently registered but untested claims that most directly test whether the largest accepted associations are context-dependent or technical artifacts. H61-H63 provide high-quality-screen robustness for SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2, and PTEN-loss/STAT3; H54 and H55 already provided analogous robustness for MSI-high/WRN and TP53-loss/USP7. H73-H76 ask whether the effects persist in the lower/median screen_roc_auc stratum, which is important because the accepted effects are unusually large and we need to know they are not confined to apparently better screens. H64, H65, H66, H67, and H72 test main effects within relevant co-alteration backgrounds: SMARCA4 loss among ARID1A-wt lines, KEAP1 loss among TP53-wt lines, TP53 loss among MYC-amplification-negative lines, PTEN loss among KEAP1-wt lines, and TP53 loss among PTEN-wt lines. The last two are especially relevant for TP53-loss/USP7, the largest accepted effect that still lacks independent validation, because they help determine whether the association is robust to common co-alterations. record.narrative: All twelve due results are confirmatory robustness/stratified-effect tests of already large accepted associations, and every one is strongly supported in the hypothesized direction. For SMARCA4 loss versus wild-type with dependency_SMARCA2 and direction -1, positive signed estimates mean the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is negative: SMARCA4-loss lines have more negative SMARCA2 scores, i.e. stronger SMARCA2 dependency. This holds in high screen_roc_auc screens (H61: +0.791, 95% CI 0.764 to 0.819), in ARID1A-wild-type lines (H64: +0.777, CI 0.756 to 0.798), and in lower/median screen_roc_auc screens (H73: +0.778, CI 0.751 to 0.805). For KEAP1 loss versus wild-type with dependency_NFE2L2 and direction +1, positive signed estimates mean KEAP1-loss lines have higher NFE2L2 scores, i.e. weaker NFE2L2 dependency. This is robust in high-quality screens (H62: +0.793, CI 0.764 to 0.822), TP53-wild-type lines (H65: +0.792, CI 0.770 to 0.815), and lower/median-quality screens (H74: +0.798, CI 0.770 to 0.827). For PTEN loss versus wild-type with dependency_STAT3 and direction -1, PTEN loss again implies stronger STAT3 dependency, persisting in high-quality screens (H63: +0.253, CI 0.181 to 0.325), KEAP1-wild-type lines (H67: +0.273, CI 0.214 to 0.332), and lower/median-quality screens (H75: +0.280, CI 0.205 to 0.355). For TP53 loss with dependency_USP7 and direction +1, TP53-loss lines have higher USP7 scores, i.e. weaker USP7 dependency, both among MYC-amplification-negative lines (H66: +0.376, CI 0.298 to 0.455) and PTEN-wild-type lines (H72: +0.388, CI 0.311 to 0.464). MSI-high with dependency_WRN remains large and negative in raw terms, or positive under direction -1, even in lower/median screen_roc_auc screens (H76: +0.790, CI 0.744 to 0.836) despite the smaller exposed cell. These effects are far beyond the practical 10% meaningfulness bar and are not plausibly explained by sampling noise. The screen_roc_auc eligibility restrictions do not appear to be outcome leakage because they are screen-quality variables rather than dependency-score variables, though they remain post-screen selection variables; conclusions are associations in the supplied dataset only. I therefore accept and close these subset/robustness claims. I request independent validation for H12, the TP53-loss/USP7 main association, because it is the largest accepted effect still lacking independent validation and is now supported by main and co-alteration-restricted subsets.

The central rationale is that the accepted effects are very large, so the most informative next question is not whether tiny additional main-effect probes are near zero, but whether the effects persist when co-altered genomic contexts and technical screen contexts differ. The proposed co-alteration main-effect tests examine SMARCA4 loss in ARID1A-loss and TP53-loss backgrounds, KEAP1 loss in TP53-loss background, PTEN loss in TP53-loss background, and TP53 loss in PTEN-wild-type background. These are complementary to prior interaction and co-restriction tests: interaction estimates are often imprecise and centered near zero, whereas direct conditional main effects tell whether the accepted contrast remains large inside a specific co-alteration stratum. The screen_roc_auc low/median robustness tests are not intended as causal claims about screen quality; they ask whether the associations are confined to apparently better screens. The CRISPR-Ky library tests ask whether the major associations are visible in a non-Avana technical setting. The new MYC-amplification/MDM2 test is restricted to TP53-wild-type cells because the MYC-MDM2-p53 axis is mechanistically most plausible there: MYC activation may create stronger MDM2 dependency when p53 signaling remains intact. This is a dataset-specific association hypothesis only, not a claim of causality or generalizability. H61-H63 provide high-quality-screen robustness for SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2, and PTEN-loss/STAT3; H54 and H55 already provided analogous robustness for MSI-high/WRN and TP53-loss/USP7. H73-H76 ask whether the effects persist in the lower/median screen_roc_auc stratum, which is important because the accepted effects are unusually large and we need to know they are not confined to apparently better screens. H64, H65, H66, H67, and H72 test main effects within relevant co-alteration backgrounds: SMARCA4 loss among ARID1A-wt lines, KEAP1 loss among TP53-wt lines, TP53 loss among MYC-amplification-negative lines, PTEN loss among KEAP1-wt lines, and TP53 loss among PTEN-wt lines. The last two are especially relevant for TP53-loss/USP7, the largest accepted effect that still lacks independent validation, because they help determine whether the association is robust to common co-alterations. No assessments are due at this stage.","appraise":"All twelve due results are confirmatory robustness/stratified-effect tests of already large accepted associations, and every one is strongly supported in the hypothesized direction. For SMARCA4 loss versus wild-type with dependency_SMARCA2 and direction -1, positive signed estimates mean the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is negative: SMARCA4-loss lines have more negative SMARCA2 scores, i.e. stronger SMARCA2 dependency. This holds in high screen_roc_auc screens (H61: +0.791, 95% CI 0.764 to 0.819), in ARID1A-wild-type lines (H64: +0.777, CI 0.756 to 0.798), and in lower/median screen_roc_auc screens (H73: +0.778, CI 0.751 to 0.805). For KEAP1 loss versus wild-type with dependency_NFE2L2 and direction +1, positive signed estimates mean KEAP1-loss lines have higher NFE2L2 scores, i.e. weaker NFE2L2 dependency. This is robust in high-quality screens (H62: +0.793, CI 0.764 to 0.822), TP53-wild-type lines (H65: +0.792, CI 0.770 to 0.815), and lower/median-quality screens (H74: +0.798, CI 0.770 to 0.827). For PTEN loss versus wild-type with dependency_STAT3 and direction -1, PTEN loss again implies stronger STAT3 dependency, persisting in high-quality screens (H63: +0.253, CI 0.181 to 0.325), KEAP1-wild-type lines (H67: +0.273, CI 0.214 to 0.332), and lower/median-quality screens (H75: +0.280, CI 0.205 to 0.355). For TP53 loss with dependency_USP7 and direction +1, TP53-loss lines have higher USP7 scores, i.e. weaker USP7 dependency, both among MYC-amplification-negative lines (H66: +0.376, CI 0.298 to 0.455) and PTEN-wild-type lines (H72: +0.388, CI 0.311 to 0.464). MSI-high with dependency_WRN remains large and negative in raw terms, or positive under direction -1, even in lower/median screen_roc_auc screens (H76: +0.790, CI 0.744 to 0.836) despite the smaller exposed cell. These effects are far beyond the practical 10% meaningfulness bar and are not plausibly explained by sampling noise. The screen_roc_auc eligibility restrictions do not appear to be outcome leakage because they are screen-quality variables rather than dependency-score variables, though they remain post-screen selection variables; conclusions are associations in the supplied dataset only. I therefore accept and close these subset/robustness claims. I request independent validation for H12, the TP53-loss/USP7 main association, because it is the largest accepted effect still lacking independent validation and is now supported by main and co-alteration-restricted subsets.","synthesize":"The newly delivered validation evidence supports the two due claims decisively. For H14, PTEN loss versus PTEN wild-type was tested with hypothesis direction -1, so a positive signed estimate corresponds to a raw negative exposed-minus-comparator contrast, meaning PTEN-loss lines have lower, i.e. more negative, STAT3 dependency scores and therefore stronger STAT3 dependency. Discovery gave a signed estimate about +0.267 with interval +0.215 to +0.319, and independent validation gave about +0.310 with interval +0.231 to +0.388. The validation interval is adjusted for the validation burden and remains far from zero. The magnitude is very large relative to the observed STAT3 score scale and standard deviation, so it far exceeds the practical 10% difference benchmark. I therefore keep H14 accepted and closed, as a dataset-specific association, not a causal or external-generalizability claim. For H8, MSI-high versus non-MSI-high also used direction -1, so signed positive estimates mean raw negative contrasts: MSI-high lines have much more negative WRN scores, i.e. stronger WRN dependency. Discovery signed estimate was about +0.790 with interval +0.760 to +0.819, and independent validation was about +0.807 with interval +0.759 to +0.855. The exposed MSI-high cell is small, but the validation effect remains enormous and precise enough that random noise or the small exposed group is not a plausible explanation. This is further supported by consistency with the high-quality-screen subset and other restrictions noted in related claims. I therefore keep H8 accepted and closed. With H8 now validated, the accepted large dataset-specific associations are SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency after reversal, PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, and MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency. The TP53-loss/USP7 association remains large and robust in the supplied dataset, including in high screen_roc_auc screens and adenocarcinoma subset, but has not yet had its own independent validation; I therefore mark H12 active as the next validation priority while leaving it accepted on existing evidence. record.narrative: Both newly delivered validation results are decisive and complete independent validation for the two most important accepted effects still lacking response. For H5, the hypothesis direction is -1, so a positive signed estimate means the raw SMARCA4-loss-minus-comparator contrast is negative; SMARCA4-loss lines have more negative dependency_SMARCA2 scores, i.e. stronger SMARCA2 dependency. The discovery effect was about +0.784 (95% CI +0.765 to +0.803), and independent validation was about +0.800 with a validation-adjusted interval +0.768 to +0.832 and adequate cell counts (364 exposed, 1636 comparator). The magnitude is roughly 2 SDs of the observed SMARCA2 score scale and far exceeds the 10% practical-significance benchmark. I therefore keep H5 accepted and close it as a strongly supported dataset-specific association, not a causal or external-generalizability claim. For H12, the hypothesis direction is +1, so positive signed estimates mean TP53-loss lines have higher dependency_USP7 scores, i.e. weaker USP7 dependency. Discovery was +0.396 (95% CI +0.325 to +0.467), and independent validation was +0.395 with validation-adjusted interval +0.293 to +0.497 (432 exposed, 1568 comparator). This is roughly one SD on the USP7 score scale, also far beyond the 10% benchmark, and it agrees with prior subsets including high screen_roc_auc, adenocarcinoma, MYC-amplification-negative, and PTEN-wild-type strata. I therefore accept H12 and close it. The major supported associations in this dataset are: SMARCA4 loss associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency (validated); KEAP1 loss associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, represented by the reversed accepted claim H17 and validated; MSI-high associated with stronger WRN dependency (validated); PTEN loss associated with stronger STAT3 dependency (validated); and TP53 loss associated with weaker USP7 dependency (now validated). Many other registered probes were near null or opposite the hypothesized direction and remain informative only as dataset-specific non-effects or underpowered small effects: for example, KRAS mutation was not meaningfully associated with KRAS dependency in H1, BRAF V600E was not associated with stronger BRAF dependency in H2, EGFR/ERBB2 amplification effects were small or inconsistent, MYC amplification was not associated with stronger DHX9, POLR2A, RPL11, or USP7 dependency, ARID1A loss was not associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, NF1 loss was not associated with stronger KRAS dependency, PTEN loss did not show meaningful associations with EGFR or ERBB2 dependency, and STK11 loss did not show meaningful association with STAT3 dependency. These rejects should be interpreted as failure to detect practically meaningful effects in this dataset, not as proof of exact biological nulls. Remaining uncertainty is mainly specificity and mechanism: interactions with lineage subtype, TP53, PIK3CA, KRAS, KEAP1, and MYC context are either near zero or imprecise and should not be promoted; small unresolved KRAS/EGFR/ERBB2/MDM2 probes are not high priority relative to the large validated effects; and direct co-alteration-restricted main effects remain untested for some accepted associations. The most informative next analysis is to run the already registered focused specificity tests, prioritizing H68 (SMARCA4 loss within ARID1A loss), H69 (SMARCA4 loss within TP53 loss), H70 (KEAP1 loss within TP53 loss), H71 (PTEN loss within TP53 loss), H77 (TP53 loss within the KY CRISPR library), H78 (SMARCA4 loss within the KY library), and H79 (MYC amplification effect on MDM2 dependency in TP53-wild-type cells). These will clarify whether the validated associations persist across important co-mutational backgrounds and a different library context. Until such evidence arrives, conclusions should remain limited to associations in the supplied lung cancer cell-line CRISPR dependency dataset, without causal interpretation or claims about broader patient cohorts.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

The central rationale is that the accepted effects are very large, so the most informative next question is not whether tiny additional main-effect probes are near zero, but whether the effects persist when co-altered genomic contexts and technical screen contexts differ. The proposed co-alteration main-effect tests examine SMARCA4 loss in ARID1A-loss and TP53-loss backgrounds, KEAP1 loss in TP53-loss background, PTEN loss in TP53-loss background, and TP53 loss in PTEN-wild-type background. These are complementary to prior interaction and co-restriction tests: interaction estimates are often imprecise and centered near zero, whereas direct conditional main effects tell whether the accepted contrast remains large inside a specific co-alteration stratum. The screen_roc_auc low/median robustness tests are not intended as causal claims about screen quality; they ask whether the associations are confined to apparently better screens. The CRISPR-Ky library tests ask whether the major associations are visible in a non-Avana technical setting. The new MYC-amplification/MDM2 test is restricted to TP53-wild-type cells because the MYC-MDM2-p53 axis is mechanistically most plausible there: MYC activation may create stronger MDM2 dependency when p53 signaling remains intact. This is a dataset-specific association hypothesis only, not a claim of causality or generalizability. H73-H76 ask whether the effects persist in the lower/median screen_roc_auc stratum, which is important because the accepted effects are unusually large and we need to know they are not confined to apparently better screens. H64, H65, H66, H67, and H72 test main effects within relevant co-alteration backgrounds: SMARCA4 loss among ARID1A-wt lines, KEAP1 loss among TP53-wt lines, TP53 loss among MYC-amplification-negative lines, PTEN loss among KEAP1-wt lines, and TP53 loss among PTEN-wt lines. The last two are especially relevant for TP53-loss/USP7, the largest accepted effect that still lacks independent validation, because they help determine whether the association is robust to common co-alterations. prompt:
Iteration 6/25, stage explore, attempt 2.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: No assessments are currently due. The strongest current dataset-specific associations are validated: SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency, PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, and TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency. The most informative next hypotheses therefore focus on specificity rather than additional near-null broad probes. I registered culture-type-adherent refinements for all five major effects, with motivating evidence attached to each parent, to ask whether the effects persist in the dominant adherent culture context rather than depending on culture heterogeneity. I also registered direct co-alteration-restricted main-effect tests: PIK3CA mutation among PTEN-wild-type cells for STAT3; TP53 loss among MYC-amplified and among KEAP1-loss cells for USP7; KEAP1 loss among PTEN-loss cells for NFE2L2; PTEN loss among KEAP1-loss cells for STAT3; SMARCA4 loss among PTEN-loss cells for SMARCA2; and MSI-high among TP53-loss cells for WRN. These tests are complementary to prior interaction analyses, which were often imprecise, by asking whether the accepted raw contrast remains large inside important genomic backgrounds. The PIK3CA/PTEN test is mechanistically motivated by PI3K-pathway activation potentially strengthening STAT3 dependency even when PTEN is intact. All new claims are hypotheses of association in the supplied lung cancer cell-line CRISPR dataset only; acceptance will require effects beyond the practical 10% meaningfulness bar and away from zero, and causal or external-generalizability interpretation remains unwarranted.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

The discovery effect was about +0.784 (95% CI +0.765 to +0.803), and independent validation was about +0.800 with a validation-adjusted interval +0.768 to +0.832 and adequate cell counts (364 exposed, 1636 comparator). The magnitude is roughly 2 SDs of the observed SMARCA2 score scale and far exceeds the 10% practical-significance benchmark. I therefore keep H5 accepted and close it as a strongly supported dataset-specific association, not a causal or external-generalizability claim. For H12, the hypothesis direction is +1, so positive signed estimates mean TP53-loss lines have higher dependency_USP7 scores, i.e. weaker USP7 dependency. Discovery was +0.396 (95% CI +0.325 to +0.467), and independent validation was +0.395 with validation-adjusted interval +0.293 to +0.497 (432 exposed, 1568 comparator). This is roughly one SD on the USP7 score scale, also far beyond the 10% benchmark, and it agrees with prior subsets including high screen_roc_auc, adenocarcinoma, MYC-amplification-negative, and PTEN-wild-type strata. record.narrative: All twelve due tests ask whether the major accepted associations remain present in important co-alteration or technical-library strata, and all provide evidence in the hypothesized direction with intervals excluding zero. For SMARCA4 loss versus SMARCA4 wild-type with dependency_SMARCA2 and direction -1, positive signed estimates indicate stronger SMARCA2 dependency among SMARCA4-loss lines; this remains very large within ARID1A-loss lines (H68: +0.814, 95% CI +0.767 to +0.862), within TP53-loss lines (H69: +0.773, CI +0.729 to +0.817), and within the KY CRISPR library (H78: +0.816, CI +0.777 to +0.856), as well as within PTEN-loss lines (H90: +0.754, CI +0.707 to +0.801). These are extremely large dataset-specific associations, roughly 2 SDs on the SMARCA2 score scale, and I accept them as robustness/subset-confirmatory results rather than causal claims. For KEAP1 loss versus KEAP1 wild-type with dependency_NFE2L2 and direction +1, positive signed estimates indicate weaker NFE2L2 dependency among KEAP1-loss lines; this holds within TP53-loss lines (H70: +0.810, CI +0.763 to +0.857) and within PTEN-loss lines (H88: +0.776, CI +0.718 to +0.834). For PTEN loss versus PTEN wild-type with dependency_STAT3 and direction -1, positive signed estimates indicate stronger STAT3 dependency among PTEN-loss lines; this remains meaningful within TP53-loss lines (H71: +0.190, CI +0.085 to +0.296) and KEAP1-loss lines (H89: +0.247, CI +0.133 to +0.361). For TP53 loss versus TP53 wild-type with dependency_USP7 and direction +1, positive signed estimates indicate weaker USP7 dependency among TP53-loss lines; this is present in MYC-amplification-positive lines (H86: +0.510, CI +0.345 to +0.674), KEAP1-loss lines (H87: +0.493, CI +0.351 to +0.635), and the KY library (H77: +0.212, CI +0.051 to +0.373). For MSI-high versus non-MSI-high with dependency_WRN and direction -1, positive signed estimates indicate stronger WRN dependency; this remains very large within TP53-loss lines (H91: +0.833, CI +0.765 to +0.900), though the exposed cell is only just above the minimum (n=24) and should be regarded as a less stable subset estimate. The main caution is that these are conditional/descriptive subset associations, not interactions unless the comparison complement is explicitly modeled, and conditioning on co-alterations can introduce collider/selection effects. I request validation only for H77 because the KY-library USP7 effect is directionally supported but materially smaller and has a lower confidence bound closer to zero than the other subset effects; validating it is informative for technical robustness. The other subset results either have very large effects or are already anchored by validated main effects, so I accept and close them as dataset-specific evidence of robustness.

For H8, MSI-high versus non-MSI-high with dependency_WRN and direction -1 was supported in discovery (+0.790, 95% CI +0.760 to +0.819) and now independently validated (+0.807, validation-adjusted 95% CI +0.759 to +0.855; n=119 vs 1881). The validation interval is comfortably away from zero and very large relative to the score scale, so I keep H8 accepted and closed as a dataset-specific association, not a causal or externally generalizable claim. For H77, TP53 loss versus TP53 wild-type with dependency_USP7 inside the KY CRISPR library and direction +1 was smaller but positive in discovery (+0.212, 95% CI +0.051 to +0.373). Independent validation was larger (+0.417, validation-adjusted 95% CI +0.210 to +0.624; n=107 vs 420). Positive signed estimates under direction +1 correspond to raw higher USP7 scores, i.e. weaker USP7 dependency among TP53-loss lines. This resolves my concern that the KY-library estimate might be an imprecise or technically context-limited signal: it is independently supported, although still smaller than the main H12 effect. I accept H77 and close it. For H40, PIK3CA mutation among PTEN-wild-type lines with dependency_STAT3 and direction -1 remains null after validation. The signed estimates are tiny and intervals include zero (discovery -0.0066, 95% CI -0.0289 to +0.0157; validation -0.0125, validation-adjusted 95% CI -0.0444 to +0.0195). There is no evidence of a practically meaningful >=10% effect or of PI3K activation through PIK3CA mutation strengthening STAT3 dependency in this dataset, so I keep H40 rejected and closed. Overall, the strongest supported associations in this dataset are now all independently validated or anchored by validated main effects: SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency (H5 validated); KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency (H17 validated, with H7 rejected as opposite); MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency (H8 validated); PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency (H14 validated); and TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency (H12 validated, with KY-library H77 now validated). Remaining uncertainty is focused on residual robustness and mechanism: culture-type dependence is still only registered, MDM2 MYC/TP53 context is untested, some lower-quality or library contexts remain untested, and subset co-alteration analyses remain associations rather than causal or formally generalized interactions. Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

prompt:
Iteration 7/25, stage explore, attempt 2.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: No assessments are due. I selected the twelve registered but untested claims that most directly extend the current robustness program around the five major dataset-specific associations: SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency, PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, and TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency. The five new screen_batch=batch_a tests H96-H100 ask whether the same main-effect contrasts persist inside the largest screen batch, which is important because batch effects are a plausible source of artifactual association. H101 complements H79 by testing whether the MYC-amplification contrast for dependency_MDM2 is attenuated among TP53-loss lines relative to TP53-wild-type lines; a positive signed estimate under direction +1 would mean the MYC contrast is less negative, i.e. weaker MDM2 dependency, in TP53-loss cells. H79 tests the MYC-amplification main effect on MDM2 within TP53-wild-type cells. H82 and H83 test whether the PTEN-loss/STAT3 and MSI-high/WRN effects persist in the dominant adherent culture type. H93-H95 test whether the KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2, PTEN-loss/STAT3, and MSI-high/WRN associations persist in the KY CRISPR library, where SMARCA2 and USP7 already have supportive checks H78 and H77. I deferred H80 and H81 because the SMARCA2 and NFE2L2 effects are already exceptionally large and validated, deferred H84 because USP7 already has both main validation and KY-library support, and deferred H92 because lower screen quality is less informative than batch, culture, library, and the focused MDM2 mechanism tests. All requested analyses remain dataset-specific association tests, not causal claims or external-generalizability claims.

record.narrative:
The twelve new results test whether the five major dataset-specific associations persist in adherent culture, the KY CRISPR library, and screen_batch=batch_a, and they also test two focused MDM2/MYC/TP53 questions. The sign convention must be read carefully: for direction -1 outcomes, positive signed estimates correspond to raw more-negative dependency scores, i.e. stronger dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1 outcomes, positive signed estimates correspond to raw higher scores, i.e. weaker dependency in the exposed group.

The major associations remain robust in the important technical and culture subsets. SMARCA4 loss remains associated with very large stronger SMARCA2 dependency within batch_a (H96: +0.747, 95% CI +0.709 to +0.785). KEAP1 loss remains associated with very large weaker NFE2L2 dependency both within the KY library (H93: +0.794, +0.752 to +0.837) and within batch_a (H97: +0.812, +0.765 to +0.858). MSI-high remains associated with very large stronger WRN dependency within adherent culture (H83: +0.813, +0.780 to +0.846), the KY library (H95: +0.732, +0.675 to +0.790), and batch_a (H98: +0.824, +0.766 to +0.882). PTEN loss remains associated with stronger STAT3 dependency within adherent culture (H82: +0.262, +0.203 to +0.321) and batch_a (H99: +0.234, +0.125 to +0.342). TP53 loss remains associated with weaker USP7 dependency within batch_a (H100: +0.417, +0.284 to +0.550). These are not causal claims or cross-batch interaction claims; they are subset associations showing that the previously validated main effects are not confined to the dominant library, a single screen quality stratum, or one co-alteration context. Conditioning on batch, culture, or library could in principle introduce collider/selection effects, but the estimates are large and intervals are far from zero, so the most parsimonious dataset-specific reading is robustness rather than artifact.

The only accepted subset effect with material uncertainty is H94: PTEN loss versus PTEN wild-type in the KY library for dependency_STAT3, +0.158, 95% CI +0.063 to +0.254, n=64 exposed. It is directionally consistent and its lower confidence bound still exceeds a practically meaningful scale relative to the STAT3 score, but it is the smallest and one of the least stable accepted subset estimates. I therefore accept it on current discovery evidence as a dataset-specific supportive subset test, but request independent validation to determine whether the PTEN-loss/STAT3 association survives this technical library context with a validation-adjusted interval.

The MDM2 tests do not currently support the planned mechanism hypothesis. H79, MYC amplification versus no MYC amplification among TP53-wild-type lines for dependency_MDM2, has a tiny signed estimate (+0.008, 95% CI -0.023 to +0.040), with the confidence interval crossing zero. H101, the MYC-amplification x TP53-loss interaction for dependency_MDM2, is also near null (+0.004, -0.071 to +0.078). Because their upper confidence bounds are not small enough to exclude a modest positive effect, I leave them unresolved rather than accepting or formally refuting a moderate interaction. However, they are not high priority for further investigation now, because the point estimates are close to zero and the existing MDM2 TP53-loss main effect was also null. The main conclusions from this update are that the five large validated associations are internally robust across adherent culture, KY-library screens, and the largest screen batch; the MDM2 MYC/TP53 follow-up is not supported by current evidence.

record.narrative: Both response-deadline/validation items support the existing major dataset-specific associations, so I keep H12 accepted and closed and now accept H94 with closed investigation. For H12, TP53 loss versus TP53 wild-type with dependency_USP7 and direction +1 was positive in discovery (+0.396, 95% CI +0.325 to +0.467) and now independently validated (+0.395, validation-adjusted 95% CI +0.293 to +0.497; n=432 vs 1568). Positive signed estimates under direction +1 correspond to raw higher USP7 dependency scores in TP53-loss lines, meaning weaker USP7 dependency. The magnitude is large relative to the USP7 score scale, and the validation interval remains clearly away from zero; I therefore keep this as a robust association in the supplied lung cancer cell-line CRISPR dataset, not as a causal or externally generalizable claim. For H94, PTEN loss versus PTEN wild-type with dependency_STAT3 inside the KY CRISPR library and direction -1 was positive in discovery (+0.158, 95% CI +0.063 to +0.254) and larger in independent validation (+0.247, validation-adjusted 95% CI +0.077 to +0.417; n=71 vs 460). Positive signed estimates under direction -1 correspond to raw lower STAT3 scores, meaning stronger STAT3 dependency among PTEN-loss lines. The validation lower bound is still meaningfully positive on the STAT3 score scale, and the effect is consistent with the already validated main PTEN-loss effect H14 and other robustness subsets; I therefore accept H94 and close it. The main supported dataset-specific findings are now: SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency (H5 validated; huge effects around +0.78 to +0.80 signed); KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency (H17 validated, while the opposite direction H7 is rejected; effects around +0.80 signed); MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency (H8 validated; effects around +0.79 to +0.81 signed); PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency (H14 validated; robust across lineage, TP53 and KEAP1 strata, screen quality, adherent culture, batch_a, and now validated KY-library H94); and TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency (H12 validated; robust across library, screen quality, lineage, and several co-alteration strata, including validated KY H77). These are associations in this supplied dataset only; many subset tests are conditional and could in principle be affected by selection or collider structure, although the repeated large effects make technical artifact unlikely. The principal negative findings are that many broad driver or alteration probes show no meaningful association: KRAS-mutation effects on KRAS/RIT1 are near null, BRAF V600E does not support stronger BRAF dependency, EGFR and ERBB2 amplifications do not support stronger EGFR or ERBB2 dependency, MYC amplification does not support stronger DHX9/POLR2A/RPL11/USP7 dependency, ARID1A loss does not support stronger SMARCA2 dependency, NF1 loss does not support stronger KRAS dependency, PTEN loss does not support EGFR or ERBB2 dependency, STK11 loss does not support stronger STAT3 dependency, media serum 10% versus 5% does not affect KIF18A dependency, and PIK3CA mutation among PTEN-wild-type lines remains null for STAT3 after validation. Remaining uncertainty is concentrated in borderline or untested items: EGFR amplification on EGFR dependency is borderline and slightly opposite the hypothesized direction, KRAS mutation on KRAS dependency remains near null, TMED10 and some culture/low-quality-library robustness tests remain unrun, MDM2 MYC/TP53 follow-up is near null and unresolved, and formal lineage-subtype interactions remain incomplete. The most informative next analysis is to test whether the five major associations are similarly present across adenocarcinoma versus non-adenocarcinoma lineage subtype. I therefore registered four new lineage-subtype interaction refinements for SMARCA4/SMARCA2, KEAP1/NFE2L2, MSI-high/WRN, and TP53-loss/USP7, while PTEN/STAT3 already has a near-null lineage interaction H36. Together with already registered H80, H81, H84, and H92, these next analyses will test internal context specificity without implying causality or generalization beyond this dataset.

record.narrative:
No assessments are due. The previous iteration strengthened the five major dataset-specific associations and left many broad probes null. The next step should distinguish true context stability from incidental context agreement by formally testing whether the effects are modified by the dominant culture condition and by screen quality, rather than only asking whether each subgroup contrast is nonzero. I therefore registered five culture-type interaction refinements for the five major associations. These compare the exposed-minus-comparator contrast among adherent cultures with the same contrast among all non-adherent culture types within the same eligible population. Under the main-effect sign convention, a nonzero interaction would mean the association is larger in one culture context than the other; a near-null interaction with tight confidence bounds would support uniformity across the dominant adherent context and the aggregate non-adherent complement. Because the complement aggregates different non-adherent conditions, a nonzero result could also reflect heterogeneity or selection rather than a clean causal culture interaction.

I also registered screen-quality interaction tests for the moderate PTEN-loss/STAT3 association and the TP53-loss/USP7 association. These ask whether the magnitude of the association depends on screen_roc_auc quality, using the median threshold 0.9555. This complements the already accepted subgroup direct tests H63 and H55: those tests show persistence within high- and low-quality strata, while the interaction tests whether the effect size differs meaningfully between them. I expect little effect modification, with the main alternatives being either a robust association independent of screen quality or a measurement-quality-dependent association.

For technical QC, I registered subset analyses restricted to lines without full matched RNA+DNA+CRISPR QC, has_rna_dna_crispr_qc=0. These are parent-linked refinements for PTEN-loss/STAT3 and TP53-loss/USP7. The scientific question is whether the associations are confined to more completely characterized lines or persist in a less QC-complete context. I anticipated persistence in the same main-effect direction, but a null or reversed subset result would suggest dataset selection or QC confounding rather than a general biological rule.

I registered two new TMED10 probes because dependency_TMED10 is currently untested. One uses SMARCA4 loss to test whether this predictor has a broader dependency association beyond SMARCA2; the other uses higher versus lower serum to test whether TMED10 dependency is culture-condition dependent. Both are exploratory with uncertain expected direction. A null result would help establish that SMARCA4-loss effects and serum effects are not generic shifts across all dependency scores. A substantial result would be a new dataset-specific association, still not causal or external.

Finally, I registered one constructed research-marker probe, marker F positivity versus marker F negativity for STAT3. This is a calibration and negative-control style comparison: marker F has no assigned biological role, so the expected raw contrast is uncertain and likely near null. If it produced a large effect on STAT3, that would be important to note as an arbitrary constructed-assay association and would encourage more caution about spurious biomarker claims. All proposed comparisons are dataset-specific associations within the supplied lung cancer cell-line CRISPR dataset; formal interaction estimates are differences in contrasts and should not be interpreted as causal interactions or generalizable biological mechanisms.

I selected 12 registered, untested hypotheses that best convert the accumulated direct subgroup robustness checks into formal context-specificity tests, while adding one broad specificity probe for the currently untested outcome dependency_TMED10. The first block, H102-H105, tests lineage-subtype interaction for SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2, KEAP1 loss/NFE2L2, MSI-high/WRN, and TP53 loss/USP7. These ask whether the already accepted main associations are similarly large in adenocarcinoma versus the non-adenocarcinoma complement. The second block, H106-H110, tests culture-context interaction for all five major associations in the same formal way, with adherent culture as the subgroup. The third block, H111-H112, tests screen-quality interaction for the two moderate associations where the high/low-screen-quality context is especially relevant: PTEN loss/STAT3 and TP53 loss/USP7. Finally, H115 tests whether SMARCA4 loss is associated with dependency_TMED10, a new outcome, to probe whether SMARCA4 loss has a highly specific SMARCA2 association or a broader generic dependency-score shift. Sign convention for the returned signed interactions: positive values mean the exposed-minus-comparator contrast is larger or more consistent with the stated hypothesis direction in the named subgroup than in the complement; negative values mean the contrast is larger in the complement; values near zero support context homogeneity. Expected result for all interactions is near null because direct subgroup tests have already been broad and mostly stable, but formal interactions will show whether effect modification is excluded with useful precision. A statistically nonzero but clinically small interaction should be interpreted cautiously, especially because the aggregate complements may contain multiple heterogeneous contexts. For H115, a near-null result would support specificity of SMARCA4 loss for SMARCA2; a substantial result would be a new dataset-specific association requiring careful appraisal and possible validation. I did not select H113-H114 QC=0 direct subsets, H116 TMED10-serum, or H117 marker-F STAT3 because the current 12-analysis budget is better spent on formal context interactions and a gene-specificity probe; they remain useful follow-ups if the present context tests reveal heterogeneity.
