8 analyze update. Selected H102-H112 plus H115. This batch tests formal effect modification by lineage subtype, culture type, and screen quality for the five major accepted associations, plus SMARCA4-loss specificity for dependency_TMED10. Priority interpretation plan: (1) Near-zero interactions with confidence intervals narrow enough to exclude a clinically meaningful difference relative to the prior effect size or ~10% benchmark support context-stable dataset-specific associations. (2) Positive interactions mean larger claimed-direction effect in the named subgroup (adenocarcinoma, adherent, or high screen quality as applicable); negative interactions mean larger in the aggregate complement. Because complements are aggregate and may contain multiple culture/library/batch structures, do not overinterpret nonzero interactions as causal context effects. (3) For H115, null TMED10/SMARCA4 supports SMARCA2-specific SMARCA4-loss association; large nonzero TMED10 effect would indicate broader dependency-score shift and should be treated as a new exploratory dataset-specific association. Not selected this iteration: H113-H114 QC=0 direct subsets, H116 TMED10-serum, H117 marker-F STAT3, H80/H81/H84 direct culture checks, H92 low-quality USP7 direct. Keep these deferred unless present interaction results indicate meaningful context modification or suggest QC/library confounding. Current accepted robust associations remain SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency, PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, and TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency, all dataset-specific and not causal/generalizable.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"No assessments are due. The previous iteration strengthened the five major dataset-specific associations and left many broad probes null. The next step should distinguish true context stability from incidental context agreement by formally testing whether the effects are modified by the dominant culture condition and by screen quality, rather than only asking whether each subgroup contrast is nonzero. I therefore registered five culture-type interaction refinements for the five major associations. These compare the exposed-minus-comparator contrast among adherent cultures with the same contrast among all non-adherent culture types within the same eligible population. Under the main-effect sign convention, a nonzero interaction would mean the association is larger in one culture context than the other; a near-null interaction with tight confidence bounds would support uniformity across the dominant adherent context and the aggregate non-adherent complement. Because the complement aggregates different non-adherent conditions, a nonzero result could also reflect heterogeneity or selection rather than a clean causal culture interaction.\n\nI also registered screen-quality interaction tests for the moderate PTEN-loss/STAT3 association and the TP53-loss/USP7 association. These ask whether the magnitude of the association depends on screen_roc_auc quality, using the median threshold 0.9555. This complements the already accepted subgroup direct tests H63 and H55: those tests show persistence within high- and low-quality strata, while the interaction tests whether the effect size differs meaningfully between them. I expect little effect modification, with the main alternatives being either a robust association independent of screen quality or a measurement-quality-dependent association.\n\nFor technical QC, I registered subset analyses restricted to lines without full matched RNA+DNA+CRISPR QC, has_rna_dna_crispr_qc=0. These are parent-linked refinements for PTEN-loss/STAT3 and TP53-loss/USP7. The scientific question is whether the associations are confined to more completely characterized lines or persist in a less QC-complete context. I anticipated persistence in the same main-effect direction, but a null or reversed subset result would suggest dataset selection or QC confounding rather than a general biological rule.\n\nI registered two new TMED10 probes because dependency_TMED10 is currently untested. One uses SMARCA4 loss to test whether this predictor has a broader dependency association beyond SMARCA2; the other uses higher versus lower serum to test whether TMED10 dependency is culture-condition dependent. Both are exploratory with uncertain expected direction. A null result would help establish that SMARCA4-loss effects and serum effects are not generic shifts across all dependency scores. A substantial result would be a new dataset-specific association, still not causal or external.\n\nFinally, I registered one constructed research-marker probe, marker F positivity versus marker F negativity for STAT3. This is a calibration and negative-control style comparison: marker F has no assigned biological role, so the expected raw contrast is uncertain and likely near null. If it produced a large effect on STAT3, that would be important to note as an arbitrary constructed-assay association and would encourage more caution about spurious biomarker claims. All proposed comparisons are dataset-specific associations within the supplied lung cancer cell-line CRISPR dataset; formal interaction estimates are differences in contrasts and should not be interpreted as causal interactions or generalizable biological mechanisms.","analyze":"No assessments are due because no new results have been added since the prior appraisal. I selected 12 registered, untested hypotheses that best convert the accumulated direct subgroup robustness checks into formal context-specificity tests, while adding one broad specificity probe for the currently untested outcome dependency_TMED10. The first block, H102-H105, tests lineage-subtype interaction for SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2, KEAP1 loss/NFE2L2, MSI-high/WRN, and TP53 loss/USP7. These ask whether the already accepted main associations are similarly large in adenocarcinoma versus the non-adenocarcinoma complement. The second block, H106-H110, tests culture-context interaction for all five major associations in the same formal way, with adherent culture as the subgroup. The third block, H111-H112, tests screen-quality interaction for the two moderate associations where the high/low-screen-quality context is especially relevant: PTEN loss/STAT3 and TP53 loss/USP7. Finally, H115 tests whether SMARCA4 loss is associated with dependency_TMED10, a new outcome, to probe whether SMARCA4 loss has a highly specific SMARCA2 association or a broader generic dependency-score shift. Sign convention for the returned signed interactions: positive values mean the exposed-minus-comparator contrast is larger or more consistent with the stated hypothesis direction in the named subgroup than in the complement; negative values mean the contrast is larger in the complement; values near zero support context homogeneity. Expected result for all interactions is near null because direct subgroup tests have already been broad and mostly stable, but formal interactions will show whether effect modification is excluded with useful precision. A statistically nonzero but clinically small interaction should be interpreted cautiously, especially because the aggregate complements may contain multiple heterogeneous contexts. For H115, a near-null result would support specificity of SMARCA4 loss for SMARCA2; a substantial result would be a new dataset-specific association requiring careful appraisal and possible validation. I did not select H113-H114 QC=0 direct subsets, H116 TMED10-serum, or H117 marker-F STAT3 because the current 12-analysis budget is better spent on formal context interactions and a gene-specificity probe; they remain useful follow-ups if the present context tests reveal heterogeneity. All selected analyses are Welch-based comparisons in the supplied dataset and support internal association/robustness conclusions only, not causality or external generalizability.","appraise":"The twelve new results test whether the five major dataset-specific associations persist in adherent culture, the KY CRISPR library, and screen_batch=batch_a, and they also test two focused MDM2/MYC/TP53 questions. The sign convention must be read carefully: for direction -1 outcomes, positive signed estimates correspond to raw more-negative dependency scores, i.e. stronger dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1 outcomes, positive signed estimates correspond to raw higher scores, i.e. weaker dependency in the exposed group.\n\nThe major associations remain robust in the important technical and culture subsets. SMARCA4 loss remains associated with very large stronger SMARCA2 dependency within batch_a (H96: +0.747, 95% CI +0.709 to +0.785). KEAP1 loss remains associated with very large weaker NFE2L2 dependency both within the KY library (H93: +0.794, +0.752 to +0.837) and within batch_a (H97: +0.812, +0.765 to +0.858). MSI-high remains associated with very large stronger WRN dependency within adherent culture (H83: +0.813, +0.780 to +0.846), the KY library (H95: +0.732, +0.675 to +0.790), and batch_a (H98: +0.824, +0.766 to +0.882). PTEN loss remains associated with stronger STAT3 dependency within adherent culture (H82: +0.262, +0.203 to +0.321) and batch_a (H99: +0.234, +0.125 to +0.342). TP53 loss remains associated with weaker USP7 dependency within batch_a (H100: +0.417, +0.284 to +0.550). These are not causal claims or cross-batch interaction claims; they are subset associations showing that the previously validated main effects are not confined to the dominant library, a single screen quality stratum, or one co-alteration context. Conditioning on batch, culture, or library could in principle introduce collider/selection effects, but the estimates are large and intervals are far from zero, so the most parsimonious dataset-specific reading is robustness rather than artifact.\n\nThe only accepted subset effect with material uncertainty is H94: PTEN loss versus PTEN wild-type in the KY library for dependency_STAT3, +0.158, 95% CI +0.063 to +0.254, n=64 exposed. It is directionally consistent and its lower confidence bound still exceeds a practically meaningful scale relative to the STAT3 score, but it is the smallest and one of the least stable accepted subset estimates. I therefore accept it on current discovery evidence as a dataset-specific supportive subset test, but request independent validation to determine whether the PTEN-loss/STAT3 association survives this technical library context with a validation-adjusted interval.\n\nThe MDM2 tests do not currently support the planned mechanism hypothesis. H79, MYC amplification versus no MYC amplification among TP53-wild-type lines for dependency_MDM2, has a tiny signed estimate (+0.008, 95% CI -0.023 to +0.040), with the confidence interval crossing zero. H101, the MYC-amplification x TP53-loss interaction for dependency_MDM2, is also near null (+0.004, -0.071 to +0.078). Because their upper confidence bounds are not small enough to exclude a modest positive effect, I leave them unresolved rather than accepting or formally refuting a moderate interaction. However, they are not high priority for further investigation now, because the point estimates are close to zero and the existing MDM2 TP53-loss main effect was also null. The main conclusions from this update are that the five large validated associations are internally robust across adherent culture, KY-library screens, and the largest screen batch; the MDM2 MYC/TP53 follow-up is not supported by current evidence.","synthesize":"Both response-deadline/validation items support the existing major dataset-specific associations, so I keep H12 accepted and closed and now accept H94 with closed investigation. For H12, TP53 loss versus TP53 wild-type with dependency_USP7 and direction +1 was positive in discovery (+0.396, 95% CI +0.325 to +0.467) and now independently validated (+0.395, validation-adjusted 95% CI +0.293 to +0.497; n=432 vs 1568). Positive signed estimates under direction +1 correspond to raw higher USP7 dependency scores in TP53-loss lines, meaning weaker USP7 dependency. The magnitude is large relative to the USP7 score scale, and the validation interval remains clearly away from zero; I therefore keep this as a robust association in the supplied lung cancer cell-line CRISPR dataset, not as a causal or externally generalizable claim. For H94, PTEN loss versus PTEN wild-type with dependency_STAT3 inside the KY CRISPR library and direction -1 was positive in discovery (+0.158, 95% CI +0.063 to +0.254) and larger in independent validation (+0.247, validation-adjusted 95% CI +0.077 to +0.417; n=71 vs 460). Positive signed estimates under direction -1 correspond to raw lower STAT3 scores, meaning stronger STAT3 dependency among PTEN-loss lines. The validation lower bound is still meaningfully positive on the STAT3 score scale, and the effect is consistent with the already validated main PTEN-loss effect H14 and other robustness subsets; I therefore accept H94 and close it. The main supported dataset-specific findings are now: SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency (H5 validated; huge effects around +0.78 to +0.80 signed); KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency (H17 validated, while the opposite direction H7 is rejected; effects around +0.80 signed); MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency (H8 validated; effects around +0.79 to +0.81 signed); PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency (H14 validated; robust across lineage, TP53 and KEAP1 strata, screen quality, adherent culture, batch_a, and now validated KY-library H94); and TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency (H12 validated; robust across library, screen quality, lineage, and several co-alteration strata, including validated KY H77). record.narrative:
The 12 new results are formal context-interaction tests for the five major accepted dataset-specific associations, plus one TMED10 specificity probe. I read signed interaction estimates as follows: a positive value means the exposed-minus-comparator contrast is larger, or more consistent with the claimed main-effect direction, in the named subgroup than in its aggregate complement; a negative value means the opposite. These are interaction contrasts, not direct mean differences, and the complements may contain heterogeneous culture/library/batch contexts, so I do not interpret them as causal context effects.

For the largest effects, lineage-subtype and culture interactions are mostly very small. H102 SMARCA4-loss x adenocarcinoma for SMARCA2 is -0.028 (95% CI -0.076 to +0.020), tiny relative to the main SMARCA2 association around +0.78 to +0.80; I reject this as evidence of meaningful adenocarcinoma-specific modification. H103 KEAP1-loss x adenocarcinoma for NFE2L2 is -0.012 (CI -0.057 to +0.033), also negligible relative to the NFE2L2 main effect around +0.80; reject. H104 MSI-high x adenocarcinoma for WRN is -0.021 (CI -0.085 to +0.042). The point is near zero, but the lower bound reaches about 10% of the main WRN effect and the non-adenocarcinoma complement is smaller, so I leave it unresolved rather than declaring a precise null. H105 TP53-loss x adenocarcinoma for USP7 is -0.038 (CI -0.190 to +0.115); this is near null in point estimate but too imprecise to exclude meaningful modification, so unresolved and deferred.

For culture context, H106 SMARCA4-loss x adherent for SMARCA2 is +0.015 (CI -0.029 to +0.058), far too small relative to the huge main SMARCA2 effect; reject. H107 KEAP1-loss x adherent for NFE2L2 is -0.019 (CI -0.064 to +0.027), small relative to the main NFE2L2 effect; reject. H108 MSI-high x adherent for WRN is the main signal: +0.105 (CI +0.037 to +0.172), statistically nonzero and suggesting that the MSI-high effect is larger in adherent culture than in the aggregate non-adherent complement. However, the lower bound corresponds to only a few percent of the main WRN effect, the non-adherent MSI-high exposed cell is only n=29, and this is one of many multiplicity-tested interactions. I therefore do not accept it as a clinically meaningful or stable interaction yet; I request independent validation of H108.

For the moderate STAT3 and USP7 associations, formal interactions are not precise enough to establish or exclude meaningful effect modification. H109 PTEN-loss x adherent for STAT3 is -0.023 (CI -0.149 to +0.104); H110 TP53-loss x adherent for USP7 is +0.080 (CI -0.094 to +0.254); H111 PTEN-loss x high screen quality for STAT3 is -0.027 (CI -0.131 to +0.076); H112 TP53-loss x high screen quality for USP7 is +0.066 (CI -0.078 to +0.209). All intervals cross zero and are wide relative to the main effects, so I leave them unresolved and deferred. Current main accepted associations remain SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency, PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, and TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency, all dataset-specific and noncausal.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"No assessments are due. The previous iteration strengthened the five major dataset-specific associations and left many broad probes null. The next step should distinguish true context stability from incidental context agreement by formally testing whether the effects are modified by the dominant culture condition and by screen quality, rather than only asking whether each subgroup contrast is nonzero. I therefore registered five culture-type interaction refinements for the five major associations. These compare the exposed-minus-comparator contrast among adherent cultures with the same contrast among all non-adherent culture types within the same eligible population. Under the main-effect sign convention, a nonzero interaction would mean the association is larger in one culture context than the other; a near-null interaction with tight confidence bounds would support uniformity across the dominant adherent context and the aggregate non-adherent complement. Because the complement aggregates different non-adherent conditions, a nonzero result could also reflect heterogeneity or selection rather than a clean causal culture interaction.\n\nI also registered screen-quality interaction tests for the moderate PTEN-loss/STAT3 association and the TP53-loss/USP7 association. These ask whether the magnitude of the association depends on screen_roc_auc quality, using the median threshold 0.9555. This complements the already accepted subgroup direct tests H63 and H55: those tests show persistence within high- and low-quality strata, while the interaction tests whether the effect size differs meaningfully between them. I expect little effect modification, with the main alternatives being either a robust association independent of screen quality or a measurement-quality-dependent association.\n\nFor technical QC, I registered subset analyses restricted to lines without full matched RNA+DNA+CRISPR QC, has_rna_dna_crispr_qc=0. These are parent-linked refinements for PTEN-loss/STAT3 and TP53-loss/USP7. The scientific question is whether the associations are confined to more completely characterized lines or persist in a less QC-complete context. I anticipated persistence in the same main-effect direction, but a null or reversed subset result would suggest dataset selection or QC confounding rather than a general biological rule.\n\nI registered two new TMED10 probes because dependency_TMED10 is currently untested. One uses SMARCA4 loss to test whether this predictor has a broader dependency association beyond SMARCA2; the other uses higher versus lower serum to test whether TMED10 dependency is culture-condition dependent. Both are exploratory with uncertain expected direction. A null result would help establish that SMARCA4-loss effects and serum effects are not generic shifts across all dependency scores. A substantial result would be a new dataset-specific association, still not causal or external.\n\nFinally, I registered one constructed research-marker probe, marker F positivity versus marker F negativity for STAT3. This is a calibration and negative-control style comparison: marker F has no assigned biological role, so the expected raw contrast is uncertain and likely near null. If it produced a large effect on STAT3, that would be important to note as an arbitrary constructed-assay association and would encourage more caution about spurious biomarker claims. All proposed comparisons are dataset-specific associations within the supplied lung cancer cell-line CRISPR dataset; formal interaction estimates are differences in contrasts and should not be interpreted as causal interactions or generalizable biological mechanisms.","analyze":"No assessments are due because no new results have been added since the prior appraisal. I selected 12 registered, untested hypotheses that best convert the accumulated direct subgroup robustness checks into formal context-specificity tests, while adding one broad specificity probe for the currently untested outcome dependency_TMED10. The first block, H102-H105, tests lineage-subtype interaction for SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2, KEAP1 loss/NFE2L2, MSI-high/WRN, and TP53 loss/USP7. These ask whether the already accepted main associations are similarly large in adenocarcinoma versus the non-adenocarcinoma complement. record.narrative:
H77 is now strongly supported and closed. TP53-loss versus TP53 wild-type in the KY CRISPR library had discovery estimate +0.212, 95% CI +0.051 to +0.373, and independent validation estimate +0.417, validation-adjusted 95% CI +0.210 to +0.624. Under the +1 hypothesis direction, positive signed estimates correspond to raw higher USP7 dependency scores, i.e. weaker USP7 dependency, in TP53-loss lines. The validation estimate is larger than discovery and the validation lower bound remains well above zero, so I keep H77 accepted as a dataset-specific association and close it. This adds library-specific robustness to the main TP53-loss/USP7 finding H12.

H40 is rejected and closed. PIK3CA mutation versus wild type among PTEN-loss wild-type lines for dependency_STAT3 was near zero in discovery, signed estimate -0.0066, 95% CI -0.0289 to +0.0157, and the independent validation was also near zero with an opposite-signed signed estimate -0.0125, validation-adjusted 95% CI -0.0444 to +0.0195. Both intervals include zero and both point estimates are negligible on the STAT3 dependency scale. I therefore do not support a clinically meaningful association of PIK3CA mutation with stronger STAT3 dependency within PTEN-wild-type lines.

H108 is rejected and closed. The discovery interaction between MSI-high status and adherent culture for dependency_WRN was positive signed +0.1046, 95% CI +0.0370 to +0.1722, suggesting a larger MSI-high effect in adherent culture than in the aggregate non-adherent complement. Independent validation did not replicate it: the signed interaction estimate became -0.0258, validation-adjusted 95% CI -0.1333 to +0.0816. The validation point estimate is small and opposite the discovery direction, and the interval crosses zero. The combined evidence does not support a stable or scientifically meaningful adherent-culture modification of the MSI-high/WRN association. I note that the validation interval is not extremely tight and still permits modest negative modification, so rejection means failure to establish a meaningful adherent-culture interaction, not proof of exact homogeneity across all non-adherent contexts.

H38 is rejected and closed. The interaction between PTEN loss and PIK3CA mutation for dependency_STAT3 was essentially null in discovery, signed estimate +0.0013, 95% CI -0.1499 to +0.1524, and the validation result was a small negative signed estimate -0.0626, validation-adjusted 95% CI -0.2523 to +0.1271. Discovery is compatible with moderate imprecision, while validation gives no positive-modification signal. The combined evidence does not support a clinically meaningful PIK3CA-mutation-specific modification of the PTEN-loss/STAT3 association. The PIK3CA subgroup cells are small, so this is best treated as a low-priority negative/unsupported interaction rather than a highly powered exact null.

Overall synthesis after these validations: the durable dataset-specific associations remain SMARCA4 loss with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, MSI-high with much stronger WRN dependency, PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, and TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency. The newly reassessed KY-library TP53/USP7 result strengthens the USP7 claim in at least one library context. Many context-interaction tests are either negligible or fail replication, including the present H108 adherent-culture WRN interaction and H38 PIK3CA/STAT3 interaction. Canonical driver probes remain largely negative or near-null, although EGFR amplification with EGFR dependency and some low-n interaction tests remain the main sources of residual uncertainty. The most useful next steps are to finish low-priority specificity and negative-control probes, especially TMED10, constructed research-marker probes, and QC or library subsets, while treating EGFR amplification as the highest-priority borderline claim if any further validation is requested.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative:
No assessments are due. The strongest supported dataset-specific associations remain SMARCA4 loss with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, MSI-high status with much stronger WRN dependency, PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, and TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency. Formal lineage and culture interactions have mostly been near null or unreliable, and the remaining unresolved interaction tests are generally too imprecise to close without creating low-value complexity. The next useful work is to test whether the large accepted associations are measurement-quality independent, technically robust, outcome-specific, and mechanistically distinguishable from simple global confounders.

I register three screen-quality interaction tests for the three largest accepted effects: SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2, KEAP1 loss/NFE2L2, and MSI-high/WRN. These compare the exposed-minus-comparator contrast among high screen_roc_auc screens with the same contrast among lower-quality screens. A positive signed interaction under the main-effect direction means the association is more consistent with the accepted direction in high-quality screens; a near-zero interaction would support independence from screen quality. A nonzero result could reflect genuine measurement-quality modification or residual batch/library heterogeneity, not causality.

I register four TMED10 specificity probes using MSI-high, KEAP1 loss, PTEN loss, and TP53 loss. TMED10 is not among the accepted associations and SMARCA4 loss was already null on TMED10. If any of these predictors produced a same-direction, meaningful shift on TMED10, that would raise concern that the predictor is associated with a broader dependency-score shift rather than an outcome-specific pattern. Null results would strengthen outcome specificity for the accepted major associations.

I register direct robustness tests of the three largest effects in lines lacking complete matched RNA+DNA+CRISPR QC, has_rna_dna_crispr_qc=0. This complements prior screen-quality, culture, lineage, batch, and library subset tests. If the effects persist, they are less likely to be confined to more completely characterized lines. If they fail, that would suggest dataset-selection or QC completeness structure rather than a general biological claim.

I register an MSI-high WRN test conditional on high mutation burden. Because MSI-high lines often have higher tumor mutational burden, testing within high mutation burden asks whether the very large MSI-high/WRN association is not merely a proxy for mutation burden. Persistence would support a repair-state or replication-stress-specific association in this dataset.

Finally, I register one new canonical predictor probe: RB1 loss versus RB1-intact for dependency_KIF18A. RB1 loss deregulates cell-cycle control and could plausibly increase dependence on mitotic regulators such as KIF18A. This is exploratory and not expected to be as large as the synthetic-lethality-like findings already observed, but it is scientifically useful broad exploration. All proposed comparisons remain associations in the supplied lung cancer cell-line CRISPR dataset, not causal or generalizable mechanisms.

The strongest supported dataset-specific associations remain SMARCA4 loss with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, MSI-high status with much stronger WRN dependency, PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, and TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency. Formal lineage and culture interactions have mostly been near null or unreliable, and the remaining unresolved interaction tests are generally too imprecise to close without creating low-value complexity. The next useful work is to test whether the large accepted associations are measurement-quality independent, technically robust, outcome-specific, and mechanistically distinguishable from simple global confounders.\n\nI register three screen-quality interaction tests for the three largest accepted effects: SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2, KEAP1 loss/NFE2L2, and MSI-high/WRN. These compare the exposed-minus-comparator contrast among high screen_roc_auc screens with the same contrast among lower-quality screens. A positive signed interaction under the main-effect direction means the association is more consistent with the accepted direction in high-quality screens; a near-zero interaction would support independence from screen quality. A nonzero result could reflect genuine measurement-quality modification or residual batch/library heterogeneity, not causality.\n\nI register four TMED10 specificity probes using MSI-high, KEAP1 loss, PTEN loss, and TP53 loss. TMED10 is not among the accepted associations and SMARCA4 loss was already null on TMED10. If any of these predictors produced a same-direction, meaningful shift on TMED10, that would raise concern that the predictor is associated with a broader dependency-score shift rather than an outcome-specific pattern. Null results would strengthen outcome specificity for the accepted major associations.\n\nI register direct robustness tests of the three largest effects in lines lacking complete matched RNA+DNA+CRISPR QC, has_rna_dna_crispr_qc=0. This complements prior screen-quality, culture, lineage, batch, and library subset tests. If the effects persist, they are less likely to be confined to more completely characterized lines. If they fail, that would suggest dataset-selection or QC completeness structure rather than a general biological claim.\n\nI register an MSI-high WRN test conditional on high mutation burden. Because MSI-high lines often have higher tumor mutational burden, testing within high mutation burden asks whether the very large MSI-high/WRN association is not merely a proxy for mutation burden. record.narrative:
I assess the 12 new results using the convention that estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction; no additional sign flip is applied. For interactions, this means the signed value measures how much the exposed-minus-comparator contrast is shifted toward the registered direction in the named subgroup relative to its complement. For the specificity probes, I judge the same-direction part of the signed interval against the outcome's typical absolute dependency-score scale; for interactions, I judge it against the corresponding main association because a clinically meaningful interaction should modify a large main effect by a nontrivial fraction.

Screen-quality interactions are unsupported for all three major associations. H118, SMARCA4-loss interaction with high screen_roc_auc for dependency_SMARCA2, is +0.0148 (95% CI -0.0240 to +0.0536). The largest same-direction modification allowed by the interval is about 0.054, roughly 7% of the SMARCA2 main association near +0.78 to +0.80. That is not scientifically meaningful interaction evidence, so I reject and close. H119, KEAP1-loss interaction with high screen quality for dependency_NFE2L2, is -0.0061 (CI -0.0465 to +0.0342), again far below 10% of the NFE2L2 main effect near +0.80; reject and close. H120, MSI-high interaction with high screen quality for dependency_WRN, is -0.0004 (CI -0.0603 to +0.0595). The point estimate is essentially zero, and the same-direction upper bound is about 0.059, only about 7.5% of the WRN main effect near +0.79; reject and close. These results strengthen the view that the three largest main associations are not driven by screen_roc_auc strata. They do not prove exact homogeneity or exclude residual library/batch confounding in low-quality screens, but there is no evidence of meaningful effect modification here.

The four TMED10 probes support outcome specificity rather than generic dependency-score shifts. H121 tests MSI-high against dependency_TMED10: signed estimate -0.0163 (CI -0.0482 to +0.0156). The same-direction upper bound is only +0.0156, roughly 6% of the absolute TMED10 mean scale about 0.25, below the 10% clinical-significance benchmark. Reject. H122 tests KEAP1 loss against dependency_TMED10: -0.0015 (CI -0.0210 to +0.0181), with same-direction maximum under 10% of the outcome scale; reject. H123 tests PTEN loss against dependency_TMED10: -0.0124 (CI -0.0360 to +0.0112); reject. H124 tests TP53 loss against dependency_TMED10: +0.0015 (CI -0.0182 to +0.0212); reject. Collectively, with the earlier SMARCA4-loss/TMED10 null, these findings make it less plausible that the accepted predictors are simply shifting many dependency scores in the same direction. This supports, but does not prove, biological outcome-specificity.

The complete-matched-QC robustness results are strong. H125, SMARCA4 loss versus intact in lines lacking complete matched RNA+DNA+CRISPR QC, is +0.7916 (CI +0.7487 to +0.8346). Under direction -1, this corresponds to much stronger SMARCA2 dependency in SMARCA4-loss lines. H126, KEAP1 loss versus intact in the QC-incomplete subset, is +0.7755 (CI +0.7290 to +0.8220) for dependency_NFE2L2; under direction +1 this corresponds to higher, i.e. weaker, NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1-loss lines. H127, MSI-high in the QC-incomplete subset, is +0.7830 (CI +0.6955 to +0.8704) for dependency_WRN under direction -1, corresponding to much stronger WRN dependency. These lower bounds remain huge and well beyond the clinical-significance threshold. I accept and close all three. H127 has only 23 MSI-high exposed cells in the QC-incomplete subset, but the effect remains extremely large and the interval is far from the 10% threshold, so acceptance is appropriate as a dataset-specific robustness result, not a generalizable mechanism.

H128 tests whether the MSI-high/WRN association is merely a proxy for high mutation burden. Within mutation_burden >= 8, MSI-high versus microsatellite-stable remains +0.7746 (CI +0.7373 to +0.8120), directionally consistent with much stronger WRN dependency. I accept and close. This reduces the concern that the MSI-high/WRN association is solely driven by global mutation burden, though residual confounding by unmeasured repair pathway activity cannot be ruled out.

H129, the new canonical RB1-loss probe for dependency_KIF18A, is near null: +0.0082 (CI -0.0193 to +0.0357). The point estimate is negligible and the interval is not compatible with a 10% meaningful effect in the hypothesized direction, so I reject and close. This is a negative canonical-driver probe in this dataset and does not establish biological irrelevance.

I request independent validation for H3 rather than any new result. EGFR amplification versus dependency_EGFR is the highest-value borderline canonical claim: discovery H3 is signed +0.0252 (CI -0.00025 to +0.0507), suggesting slightly stronger EGFR dependency in amplified lines, with a point estimate around 10% of the absolute mean EGFR dependency scale and a CI barely crossing zero. Because many multiplicity-tested claims have already been rejected or supported by much larger effects, confirming or eliminating this borderline canonical signal is the most useful use of the remaining validation capacity.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

The next useful work is to test whether the large accepted associations are measurement-quality independent, technically robust, outcome-specific, and mechanistically distinguishable from simple global confounders.\n\nI register three screen-quality interaction tests for the three largest accepted effects: SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2, KEAP1 loss/NFE2L2, and MSI-high/WRN. These compare the exposed-minus-comparator contrast among high screen_roc_auc screens with the same contrast among lower-quality screens. A positive signed interaction under the main-effect direction means the association is more consistent with the accepted direction in high-quality screens; a near-zero interaction would support independence from screen quality. A nonzero result could reflect genuine measurement-quality modification or residual batch/library heterogeneity, not causality.\n\nI register four TMED10 specificity probes using MSI-high, KEAP1 loss, PTEN loss, and TP53 loss. TMED10 is not among the accepted associations and SMARCA4 loss was already null on TMED10. This complements prior screen-quality, culture, lineage, batch, and library subset tests. If the effects persist, they are less likely to be confined to more completely characterized lines. If they fail, that would suggest dataset-selection or QC completeness structure rather than a general biological claim.\n\nI register an MSI-high WRN test conditional on high mutation burden. Because MSI-high lines often have higher tumor mutational burden, testing within high mutation burden asks whether the very large MSI-high/WRN association is not merely a proxy for mutation burden. H118-H120 are formal screen_roc_auc interactions for SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2, KEAP1 loss/NFE2L2, and MSI-high/WRN. These ask whether the large direct associations differ between high-quality and lower-quality screen strata. For these signed interactions, a near-zero estimate supports screen-quality-independent association in this dataset; a positive estimate means the contrast is more consistent with the stated main-effect direction in the high-AUC stratum, while a negative estimate means it is more consistent in the complement. Given prior high/low direct subgroup results, I expect these to be near null but potentially imprecise for the smaller cells, especially WRN. H121-H124 test TMED10 as an additional unrelated dependency score for MSI-high, KEAP1 loss, PTEN loss, and TP53 loss. Because SMARCA4 loss was already null on TMED10 in H115, these tests probe whether the accepted predictors cause a broad dependency-score shift. Null results would strengthen outcome specificity; substantial same-direction shifts would warrant caution about generic effects. H125-H127 test whether the three largest associations persist among lines lacking complete matched RNA+DNA+CRISPR QC, has_rna_dna_crispr_qc=0. This complements screen-quality, culture, lineage, library, and batch tests and asks whether the effects are confined to more completely characterized lines. H128 tests MSI-high association with WRN within high mutation burden, a useful specificity check because MSI-high lines often have higher TMB. If the WRN effect remains large under high TMB, it is less likely to be merely a proxy for global mutation burden. All selected comparisons are Welch-based analyses in the supplied dataset and support association or robustness conclusions only, not causal mechanisms or external generalizability.","appraise":"I assess the 12 new results using the convention that estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction; no additional sign flip is applied. For interactions, this means the signed value measures how much the exposed-minus-comparator contrast is shifted toward the registered direction in the named subgroup relative to its complement. For the specificity probes, I judge the same-direction part of the signed interval against the outcome's typical absolute dependency-score scale; for interactions, I judge it against the corresponding main association because a clinically meaningful interaction should modify a large main effect by a nontrivial fraction.\n\nScreen-quality interactions are unsupported for all three major associations. H118, SMARCA4-loss interaction with high screen_roc_auc for dependency_SMARCA2, is +0.0148 (95% CI -0.0240 to +0.0536). The largest same-direction modification allowed by the interval is about 0.054, roughly 7% of the SMARCA2 main association near +0.78 to +0.80. That is not scientifically meaningful interaction evidence, so I reject and close. H119, KEAP1-loss interaction with high screen quality for dependency_NFE2L2, is -0.0061 (CI -0.0465 to +0.0342), again far below 10% of the NFE2L2 main effect near +0.80; reject and close. H120, MSI-high interaction with high screen quality for dependency_WRN, is -0.0004 (CI -0.0603 to +0.0595). The point estimate is essentially zero, and the same-direction upper bound is about 0.059, only about 7.5% of the WRN main effect near +0.79; reject and close. These results strengthen the view that the three largest main associations are not driven by screen_roc_auc strata. They do not prove exact homogeneity or exclude residual library/batch confounding in low-quality screens, but there is no evidence of meaningful effect modification here.\n\nThe four TMED10 probes support outcome specificity rather than generic dependency-score shifts. H121 tests MSI-high against dependency_TMED10: signed estimate -0.0163 (CI -0.0482 to +0.0156). The same-direction upper bound is only +0.0156, roughly 6% of the absolute TMED10 mean scale about 0.25, below the 10% clinical-significance benchmark. Reject. H122 tests KEAP1 loss against dependency_TMED10: -0.0015 (CI -0.0210 to +0.0181), with same-direction maximum under 10% of the outcome scale; reject. H123 tests PTEN loss against dependency_TMED10: -0.0124 (CI -0.0360 to +0.0112); reject. H124 tests TP53 loss against dependency_TMED10: +0.0015 (CI -0.0182 to +0.0212); reject. Collectively, with the earlier SMARCA4-loss/TMED10 null, these findings make it less plausible that the accepted predictors are simply shifting many dependency scores in the same direction. This supports, but does not prove, biological outcome-specificity.\n\nThe complete-matched-QC robustness results are strong. H125, SMARCA4 loss versus intact in lines lacking complete matched RNA+DNA+CRISPR QC, is +0.7916 (CI +0.7487 to +0.8346). Under direction -1, this corresponds to much stronger SMARCA2 dependency in SMARCA4-loss lines. H126, KEAP1 loss versus intact in the QC-incomplete subset, is +0.7755 (CI +0.7290 to +0.8220) for dependency_NFE2L2; under direction +1 this corresponds to higher, i.e. weaker, NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1-loss lines. H127, MSI-high in the QC-incomplete subset, is +0.7830 (CI +0.6955 to +0.8704) for dependency_WRN under direction -1, corresponding to much stronger WRN dependency. These lower bounds remain huge and well beyond the clinical-significance threshold. I accept and close all three. H127 has only 23 MSI-high exposed cells in the QC-incomplete subset, but the effect remains extremely large and the interval is far from the 10% threshold, so acceptance is appropriate as a dataset-specific robustness result, not a generalizable mechanism.\n\nH128 tests whether the MSI-high/WRN association is merely a proxy for high mutation burden. Within mutation_burden >= 8, MSI-high versus microsatellite-stable remains +0.7746 (CI +0.7373 to +0.8120), directionally consistent with much stronger WRN dependency. I accept and close. This reduces the concern that the MSI-high/WRN association is solely driven by global mutation burden, though residual confounding by unmeasured repair pathway activity cannot be ruled out.\n\nH129, the new canonical RB1-loss probe for dependency_KIF18A, is near null: +0.0082 (CI -0.0193 to +0.0357). The point estimate is negligible and the interval is not compatible with a 10% meaningful effect in the hypothesized direction, so I reject and close. This is a negative canonical-driver probe in this dataset and does not establish biological irrelevance.\n\nI request independent validation for H3 rather than any new result. EGFR amplification versus dependency_EGFR is the highest-value borderline canonical claim: discovery H3 is signed +0.0252 (CI -0.00025 to +0.0507), suggesting slightly stronger EGFR dependency in amplified lines, with a point estimate around 10% of the absolute mean EGFR dependency scale and a CI barely crossing zero. record.narrative: No assessments are due. I register ten follow-up comparisons that prioritize the highest-value unresolved and newly accepted results. First, I test robustness and specificity for the accepted major associations: SMARCA4 loss with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, MSI-high status with much stronger WRN dependency, PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, and TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency. For each expected direction below, 'raw lower' means more negative dependency scores and thus stronger dependency, while 'raw higher' means less negative or positive scores and thus weaker dependency. Second, I test two receptor-pathway questions that remain scientifically unresolved: whether KRAS-mutant lines show a small true gain in KRAS dependency in more completely characterized lines, and whether ERBB2 amplification or PIK3CA mutation alter dependency on ERBB2/EGFR in a pathway-consistent manner. If PIK3CA mutation weakens upstream receptor dependency, raw scores for ERBB2 and EGFR should be higher; if it instead strengthens dependency or reflects co-driver heterogeneity, the raw difference could be lower or null. Third, I test mutation-burden strata to determine whether accepted effects are not merely proxies for TMB: USP7/TP53 and STAT3/PTEN are tested in higher TMB lines, while NFE2L2/KEAP1 and WRN/MSI-high are tested in lower/moderate TMB lines. Persistence in the named stratum would support robustness of the association in this dataset; attenuation or failure would suggest TMB-correlated structure. Fourth, I test the most common Avana CRISPR library directly for two accepted effects because KY-library subset robustness has already been shown but Avana-specific confirmation is not yet complete. These are association tests only; they do not establish causality or external generalizability.

These ask whether the large direct associations differ between high-quality and lower-quality screen strata. For these signed interactions, a near-zero estimate supports screen-quality-independent association in this dataset; a positive estimate means the contrast is more consistent with the stated main-effect direction in the high-AUC stratum, while a negative estimate means it is more consistent in the complement. For the specificity probes, I judge the same-direction part of the signed interval against the outcome's typical absolute dependency-score scale; for interactions, I judge it against the corresponding main association because a clinically meaningful interaction should modify a large main effect by a nontrivial fraction.\n\nScreen-quality interactions are unsupported for all three major associations. They are not expected to be large, but informative as negative or cross-driver checks against the main associations. Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. The QC-incomplete robustness probes remained large and precise: PTEN loss is associated with lower dependency_STAT3 by +0.217 (95% CI +0.105 to +0.329) among matched-QC-incomplete lines, and TP53 loss with higher, i.e. weaker, dependency_USP7 by +0.428 (95% CI +0.271 to +0.586); accept and close because the lower bounds exceed the 10% absolute-dependency benchmark by a wide margin. H134 remains unresolved: complete-QC KRAS-mutant lines show only +0.016 (95% CI -0.003 to +0.036) for dependency_KRAS, smaller than a canonical effect would be and below the 10% point benchmark, although the upper bound is borderline; because several KRAS probes are weak and validation would be imprecise for a small effect, I defer it rather than request validation. The specificity probes are unsupported: KRAS mutation for BRAF dependency in the registered positive direction is actually negative and null (H131 -0.016, CI -0.034 to +0.001); ERBB2 amplification for EGFR dependency is near null (H133 +0.003, CI -0.023 to +0.030); and ERBB2 amplification for ERBB2 dependency among EGFR-amplification-negative lines is essentially zero (H135 +0.001, CI -0.028 to +0.030); reject and close these as unsupported in this dataset. The mutation-burden and Avana-library strata show that the large accepted associations persist: TP53 loss versus intact for dependency_USP7 is +0.546 (CI +0.422 to +0.670) in high mutation burden; KEAP1 loss versus intact for dependency_NFE2L2 is +0.795 (CI +0.771 to +0.818) in lower/moderate mutation burden; MSI-high for dependency_WRN is +0.800 (CI +0.745 to +0.854) in lower/moderate mutation burden; PTEN loss for dependency_STAT3 is +0.276 (CI +0.181 to +0.371) in high mutation burden; SMARCA4 loss for dependency_SMARCA2 is +0.781 (CI +0.760 to +0.802) and KEAP1 loss for dependency_NFE2L2 is +0.796 (CI +0.774 to +0.818) in the Avana library. All lower bounds are far above the clinical-significance threshold, so accept and close. These subset tests reduce concern that the main effects are proxies for mutation burden or library-specific artifacts, but they remain dataset-specific associations and do not establish causality or external generalizability. I request no validation now because the newly accepted results are already large and robust, and the only borderline canonical effect, H134, is small enough that validation is unlikely to support a clinically meaningful KRAS-dependency gain.

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

record.narrative: The due validations do not support the two context interactions they were testing. For H108, the culture-type adherent interaction on MSI-high/dependency_WRN was initially positive signed in discovery, +0.1046, 95% CI +0.037 to +0.172, but independent validation reversed and nullified the interaction, -0.0258, validation-adjusted CI -0.133 to +0.082. The validation interval excludes clinically meaningful positive interaction while including zero, so I reject H108 and close it. This does not threaten the robust main MSI-high/WRN association. For H38, the PIK3CA interaction on PTEN-loss/dependency_STAT3 was near null in discovery, +0.0013, CI -0.150 to +0.152, and validation was small and opposite signed, -0.0626, adjusted CI -0.252 to +0.127. PIK3CA status does not appear to modify the broader PTEN-loss/STAT3 association; H38 remains rejected and closed. I also converted several previously deferred null or small directional claims to closed rejects where their independent intervals do not plausibly support a clinically meaningful effect: KRAS-mutation gain in KRAS dependency, complete-QC KRAS-mutation KRAS dependency, adenocarcinoma-restricted KRAS and EGFR amplification probes, ERBB2-amplification/dependency_ERBB2, MDM2/TP53 and MDM2/MYC probes, WRN/BRCA2, and several narrow upper-bound null interactions. With these updates, the dataset-supported findings are the five large, repeated associations: SMARCA4 loss with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, KEAP1 loss with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency, MSI-high status with much stronger WRN dependency, PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, and TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency. These persist across matched-QC status, screen-quality strata, mutation-burden strata, CRISPR libraries, screen batches, culture subsets, and several specificity probes, with negligible or nonreplicated context interactions. Negative or unsupported findings now include canonical EGFR amplification, ERBB2 amplification, PIK3CA/STAT3 under PTEN-intact context, PIK3CA modification of PTEN/STAT3, KRAS gain of KRAS dependency, MYC effects on DHX9/POLR2A/RPL11/USP7, RB1/KIF18A, ARID1A/SMARCA2, WRN/BRCA2, MDM2/TP53 or MDM2/MYC, and cross-driver receptor probes. Remaining uncertainty is mainly low-value or technically/culturally unresolved probes: TMED10 media-serum and MYC probes, research-marker F/STAT3, ERBB2 cross-driver and PIK3CA active probes, and some wide-null interactions where intervals cannot rule out a modest effect. The most informative next analysis is to complete the active media, marker, TMED10, and cross-driver probes plus the newly proposed complementary mutation-burden robustness tests. I request no new validation now; the two validation slots should be reserved unless an active probe produces a clinically meaningful point estimate with an interval that leaves ambiguity.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative:
No assessments are due. I register 11 new comparisons focused on two complementary needs: (1) completing biologically targeted probes of key dependency outcomes, especially WRN and BRAF, and (2) testing whether the five durable accepted associations are homogeneous across KRAS-mutant versus KRAS-wild-type lung-adenocarcinoma context. KRAS co-mutation status is important because it represents a major oncogenic state and may modify synthetic-lethal effects through replication stress, proliferative pressure, or pathway rewiring.

For dependency_BRAF, the overall BRAF V600E probe H2 was null, but this could partly reflect mixing of genetically distinct subgroups. I now restrict comparison to KRAS-wild-type lines, where a BRAF V600E-specific dependency should be more interpretable if it exists. I expect raw lower (stronger) dependency in BRAF-mutant lines under this restriction, but the main alternative remains no driver-specific effect in this dataset.

For dependency_WRN, RB1 loss and MYC amplification are plausible replication-stress modifiers. RB1 loss may increase replication stress and therefore raw lower WRN dependency; MYC amplification has a similar synthetic-lethal rationale, although earlier MYC probes for DHX9/POLR2A/RPL11 were null, so uncertainty is substantial. TP53 loss is included with an uncertain expectation because TP53 loss may increase replication stress and WRN dependency, but WRN's dominant context here is MSI status rather than p53 pathway status. For dependency_STAT3, MYC amplification is tested as a transcriptional/proliferative modifier with no expected direction yet; a null would be consistent with the current picture that STAT3 dependency is linked mainly to PTEN loss rather than broad oncogene amplification.

The co-mutation stratification tests are not mere repetitions. They ask whether the accepted associations are driver-context-specific or broadly robust. I register KRAS-mutant and KRAS-wild-type strata where cells are expected to have adequate n. For the accepted directions: SMARCA4 loss should remain associated with raw lower (stronger) SMARCA2 dependency; KEAP1 loss should remain associated with raw higher (weaker) NFE2L2 dependency; TP53 loss should remain associated with raw higher (weaker) USP7 dependency; MSI-high should remain associated with raw lower (stronger) WRN dependency; and PTEN loss should remain associated with raw lower (stronger) STAT3 dependency. Similar effects across KRAS states would support robustness; attenuation or reversal in one state would suggest co-driver modification and should not be interpreted as causal without validation. All conclusions remain dataset-specific associations on CRISPR dependency scales, not generalizable mechanisms.

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without

Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
