record.narrative:
Assessment of the due response: H189 asked whether the PTEN-loss -> stronger STAT3 dependency association is amplified in high EMT-score lines. The discovery interaction was borderline and imprecise: signed estimate +0.117, 95% CI -0.006 to +0.241. Independent validation did not replicate the hypothesized direction: signed estimate -0.060, independent 95% interval -0.222 to +0.102. The validation interval includes zero and is compatible with no modification or an opposite-direction modification. Because the effect is neither directionally replicated nor clinically meaningful at the supplied 10% relative-difference benchmark, H189 is rejected and closed. This does not overturn the main PTEN-loss -> STAT3 association; it only fails to support EMT-high status as a scope-narrowing modifier in this dataset.

Current supported scientific picture: the evidence supports five large, outcome-specific, dataset-specific CRISPR dependency-score associations, each with independent validation. SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency: signed discovery effect +0.784 (95% CI +0.765 to +0.803) and independent validation +0.800 (independent interval +0.768 to +0.832); the raw exposed-minus-comparator difference is correspondingly negative. KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, i.e. higher/less negative dependency scores: signed accepted effect +0.796 (95% CI +0.776 to +0.816) and independent validation +0.800 (independent interval +0.772 to +0.829). MSI-high status is associated with much stronger WRN dependency: signed discovery effect +0.790 (95% CI +0.760 to +0.819) and independent validation +0.807 (independent interval +0.759 to +0.855). PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency: signed discovery effect +0.267 (95% CI +0.215 to +0.319) and independent validation +0.310 (independent interval +0.231 to +0.388). TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency: signed discovery effect +0.396 (95% CI +0.325 to +0.467) and independent validation +0.395 (independent interval +0.293 to +0.497). These effects are far larger than the practical 10% relative-difference benchmark and are internally consistent across many accepted measured contexts, including mutation-burden strata, screen-quality strata, culture batches, proliferation-rate strata, and several genomic or technical subgroup contexts.

Negative and nonreplicated findings: the simple receptor-driver hypotheses are not supported. KRAS mutation does not credibly increase KRAS dependency; BRAF V600E does not credibly increase BRAF dependency; EGFR amplification does not support EGFR dependency and its validation did not recover a positive signal; ERBB2 amplification is null for ERBB2 dependency. Broad MYC-amplification probes, arbitrary research markers, and many cross-pathway or receptor/TMED10 probes are also null or unsupported. Interaction probes are generally negative or nonreplicated: high mutation burden did not validate as a modifier of TP53-loss USP7 dependency (H168); culture-type did not validate as a modifier of MSI-high WRN dependency (H108); fast proliferation did not support a WRN interaction (H190); and now EMT-high status does not validate as a modifier of PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency (H189). Specificity probes support outcome specificity for the accepted core effects: TP53 loss is not meaningfully associated with SMARCA2 dependency, STK11 loss is null for NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1-wildtype lines, and BRCA2 loss is near-null for POLR2A and DHX9 dependency.

Unresolved uncertainty: the five accepted associations remain associations in this supplied lung cancer cell-line CRISPR dataset, not causal claims or generalized biological claims. Residual confounding, screen-quality effects, population composition, and dataset-specific technical structure could contribute. Several untested specificity probes remain useful, especially H186-H188, which test whether accepted exposure-outcome effects spill over to related but non-matching dependencies. Validation capacity is exhausted, so future work should focus on high-value discovery specificity and context probes rather than new independent validation requests.

Most informative next analysis: I activated the three remaining cross-specificity probes H186, H187, and H188, and registered a focused median-dichotomized aneuploidy interaction panel for the five accepted associations. These are better than broad scanning because they directly test whether genomic-aneuploidy context modifies already robust associations. I would accept an aneuploidy interaction only if the signed estimate is scientifically meaningful, roughly at least 0.1 dependency-score units in magnitude, and its interval excludes the null. If the interaction panel is null, that further supports context-invariant dataset-specific structure and favors closing the broad interaction search while retaining the five accepted associations as the core scientific result.

record.narrative: No discovery assessments are due. I registered nine scientifically focused probes to complete internal validation of the accepted dependency associations and their outcome specificity, while deferring the newly registered aneuploidy-interaction panel so that the active pool prioritizes direct context and specificity tests. First, the five accepted associations were previously confirmed in fast-proliferation contexts at growth_rate_doublings_per_day >= 0.5. I now test the complementary slow-proliferation context, growth_rate_doublings_per_day <= 0.4, for SMARCA4 loss with SMARCA2 dependency, KEAP1 loss with NFE2L2 dependency, MSI-high status with WRN dependency, PTEN loss with STAT3 dependency, and TP53 loss with USP7 dependency. These are population-restricted main contrasts in the same lung cancer line data. Expected raw directions match the accepted claims: SMARCA4-loss and MSI-high lines should have more negative dependency scores for SMARCA2 and WRN; PTEN-loss lines should have more negative STAT3 dependency scores; KEAP1-loss and TP53-loss lines should have higher, less negative scores for NFE2L2 and USP7, respectively. If the signed effects remain large and the intervals exclude the null, this supports context-specific robustness within this dataset. If they shrink substantially or become compatible with trivial effects, that would indicate proliferation-rate dependence. Second, I registered four cross-specificity probes to test whether the accepted predictors have broad effects on other dependencies: PTEN loss on SMARCA2, SMARCA4 loss on STAT3, TP53 loss on STAT3, and KEAP1 loss on USP7. For these, the anticipated raw contrast is null. A large effect in the hypothesized direction would be a new association and would complicate the current outcome-specific picture; a near-null effect supports specificity of the accepted effects. I will accept a specificity spillover only if the signed effect corresponds to at least the 10% relative-difference benchmark and its interval excludes both the null and a trivial range. The aneuploidy interaction panel is deferred rather than closed because validation capacity is exhausted and most interaction hypotheses have been null or nonreplicated; direct slow-growth stratum tests and cross-specificity tests are more immediately informative. All conclusions remain dataset-specific associations, not causal or generalized biological claims.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released

record.narrative: No assessments are due in this analyze stage, so I do not change any existing claim status. I request analyses for the 12 active, registered comparisons that most directly complete the current context and outcome-specificity program. The first five test whether the five accepted large associations remain scientifically meaningful in a slow-proliferation context, growth_rate_doublings_per_day <= 0.4: H214 SMARCA4 loss with SMARCA2 dependency, H215 KEAP1 loss with NFE2L2 dependency, H216 MSI-high with WRN dependency, H217 PTEN loss with STAT3 dependency, and H218 TP53 loss with USP7 dependency. These complement the previously tested faster-proliferation context. For these main context probes, I will accept only if the signed estimate remains clearly in the registered direction, the 95% Welch interval excludes zero, and the magnitude is scientifically meaningful, using roughly 0.1 dependency-score units as a practical threshold. The next four probes test new cross-specificity of the accepted exposures on non-matching outcomes: H219 PTEN loss on SMARCA2 dependency, H220 SMARCA4 loss on STAT3 dependency, H221 TP53 loss on STAT3 dependency, and H222 KEAP1 loss on USP7 dependency. These are expected to be null if the accepted effects are outcome-specific; a large, precise effect would complicate the specificity picture. The final three are existing active specificity controls: H186 KEAP1 loss on SMARCA2 dependency, H187 PTEN loss on WRN dependency, and H188 SMARCA4 loss on WRN dependency. I interpret these as specificity tests rather than primary biological hypotheses: a near-null result supports the current outcome-specific interpretation, whereas a large effect would indicate broader pathway-level associations. The median-dichotomized aneuploidy interaction panel remains deferred because validation capacity is exhausted and the most informative remaining questions are direct slow-growth context replication and outcome specificity.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All twelve due discovery results are interpreted as signed estimates for the registered direction. H214-H218 are context-replication probes for the five core accepted associations in the complementary slow-proliferation stratum (growth_rate_doublings_per_day <= 0.4). Each has a large signed estimate, a 95% Welch interval excluding zero, and a magnitude far above the practical 10% relative-difference benchmark: SMARCA4 loss vs SMARCA2 dependency +0.795 [0.757, 0.834]; KEAP1 loss vs NFE2L2 dependency +0.790 [0.755, 0.825]; MSI-high vs WRN dependency +0.815 [0.758, 0.872]; PTEN loss vs STAT3 dependency +0.261 [0.161, 0.360]; TP53 loss vs USP7 dependency +0.416 [0.291, 0.542]. All cells satisfy the minimum-n rule. These acceptances are dataset-specific replication statements, not causal or generalizable claims, but they materially strengthen the internal consistency of the five core associations across proliferation contexts. The null/nonreplicated specificity probes do not support broad spillover: H219 PTEN loss on SMARCA2 +0.018 [-0.029, 0.065], H220 SMARCA4 loss on STAT3 -0.005 [-0.032, 0.022], H221 TP53 loss on STAT3 -0.012 [-0.037, 0.012], H222 KEAP1 loss on USP7 +0.030 [-0.014, 0.074], H186 KEAP1 loss on SMARCA2 -0.006 [-0.046, 0.034], H187 PTEN loss on WRN +0.003 [-0.031, 0.038], and H188 SMARCA4 loss on WRN +0.003 [-0.026, 0.032]. Expected raw directions match the accepted claims: SMARCA4-loss and MSI-high lines should have more negative dependency scores for SMARCA2 and WRN; PTEN-loss lines should have more negative STAT3 dependency scores; KEAP1-loss and TP53-loss lines should have higher, less negative scores for NFE2L2 and USP7, respectively. If they shrink substantially or become compatible with trivial effects, that would indicate proliferation-rate dependence. Second, I registered four cross-specificity probes to test whether the accepted predictors have broad effects on other dependencies: PTEN loss on SMARCA2, SMARCA4 loss on STAT3, TP53 loss on STAT3, and KEAP1 loss on USP7. For these, the anticipated raw contrast is null. A large effect in the hypothesized direction would be a new association and would complicate the current outcome-specific picture; a near-null effect supports specificity of the accepted effects. record.narrative:
The twelve due results are interpreted as signed estimates for their registered directions. H209-H213 are median-dichotomized aneuploidy-interaction probes for the five core accepted associations. None of these interactions provides evidence for the registered direction of effect modification: every 95% Welch interval includes zero, and the point estimates are small relative to the corresponding main effects and to the practical significance scale. For H213, the point estimate is actually opposite the registered positive direction, and the interval remains compatible with effects in both directions; I therefore reject the claimed positive interaction while explicitly not asserting that the true interaction is exactly zero. More generally, these null interaction results do not prove absence of all context modification, especially because dichotomizing at the median can reduce sensitivity and hide nonlinear or threshold effects. However, given that the complementary high-context direct tests below replicate the core effects, there is little reason to continue prioritizing these interaction probes.

H223-H227 are direct high-aneuploidy stratum tests of the five accepted core associations. All have signed estimates in the registered direction, intervals that exclude zero, cell sizes satisfying the minimum-n rule, and magnitudes that remain large and comparable to the overall effects: SMARCA4 loss on SMARCA2 dependency +0.775 [0.747, 0.803]; KEAP1 loss on NFE2L2 dependency +0.794 [0.766, 0.822]; MSI-high on WRN dependency +0.801 [0.761, 0.841]; PTEN loss on STAT3 dependency +0.278 [0.203, 0.353]; TP53 loss on USP7 dependency +0.359 [0.259, 0.460]. These effects far exceed the 10% relative-difference practical benchmark on the outcome scale and are consistent with the earlier accepted core associations. I accept them as dataset-specific internal replication in high-aneuploidy context and close these refinement investigations.

H228-H229 test whether the accepted PTEN-loss STAT3 effect and KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 effect persist in high IFN-gamma-signature or high-hypoxia contexts. Both replicate strongly: PTEN loss on STAT3 dependency +0.428 [0.326, 0.529] in IFN-high lines, and KEAP1 loss on NFE2L2 dependency +0.779 [0.738, 0.821] in hypoxia-high lines. These intervals exclude zero and the estimates are scientifically meaningful. I accept them as dataset-specific replication/scope evidence, not causal or externally generalizable claims.

Multiplicity is modestly controlled by treating H223-H229 as pre-specified replication of already accepted core effects rather than a broad new discovery scan; all accepted results are large and precise, not borderline. The interaction nulls are treated as failures to support the specific registered modifications, not as proof of strict nullity. Validation capacity is exhausted, so no validation is requested. The evidence remains confined to the supplied dataset and does not establish causal mechanisms or generalizability to other cohorts, screen platforms, or therapeutic settings.

4. PTEN loss is associated with increased STAT3 dependency. Accepted signed contrasts are about +0.267 discovery and +0.310 validation, corresponding to more negative STAT3 scores in PTEN-loss lines. The effect is replicated across many strata and remains meaningful in high aneuploidy, high IFN-gamma, high and low growth rate, high and low screen quality, Avana library, batch_a, adherent culture, matched-omics missing, mutation-burden strata, and KRAS status. It is not credibly amplified by EMT, PIK3CA mutation, TP53 loss, aneuploidy, growth, screen quality, culture type, or mutation burden in the tested contrasts.

Accepted signed contrasts are about +0.396 discovery and +0.395 validation, corresponding to higher or less negative USP7 scores in TP53-loss lines. The effect is replicated across many contexts and remains about +0.21 to +0.55 across tested strata. The independent validation R193 gives a signed interaction of -0.0599 with 99.6 percent interval -0.2215 to 0.1018 against a registered negative PTEN-loss STAT3 interaction in EMT-high lines, while discovery R182 was +0.1175 with 95 percent interval -0.0060 to 0.2410. Both intervals include zero, and the validation point estimate is opposite the registered direction, so H189 remains rejected and closed. This argues against the hypothesis that high EMT score amplifies the PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency association. No new voluntary validation remains, and the accepted claim set is unchanged. The final scientific synthesis is that five outcome-specific associations are robustly supported in this dataset: SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency, PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, and TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency. These associations are large, internally replicated across multiple strata, and not credibly modified by the tested context variables, including EMT score. Most driver-lineage simple dependency hypotheses, research-marker associations, and interaction modifiers remain negative or unsupported.

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without

record.narrative: All twelve due results are signed to the registered hypothesis direction. H230 supports a persistent PTEN-loss STAT3-dependency association in the IFN-low complement: signed estimate +0.207 [0.148, 0.266], with every cell meeting the minimum-size rule and the interval excluding zero. H231 then gives a precise positive signed interaction for the registered IFN-high effect-modification claim: +0.221 [0.104, 0.338]. Combined with the earlier direct high-IFN result (+0.428 [0.326, 0.529]), this is internally consistent with amplification of the PTEN-loss STAT3 association in IFN-high relative to IFN-low lines. record.narrative: No new validation evidence was released in this synthesis and no claim assessments are due. I therefore synthesize the cumulative discovery and validation evidence. The strongest and most defensible conclusions are dataset-specific CRISPR dependency associations, not causal claims. 1. SMARCA4 loss is robustly associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency. The accepted core estimate H5/R5 is a signed +0.784 (95% interval 0.765 to 0.803), which corresponds to SMARCA4-loss cells having a raw dependency score about 0.78 units lower, i.e. more negative, than SMARCA4-intact cells. Independent validation is nearly identical, H5/R39 +0.800 (validated interval 0.768 to 0.832), and the association replicates across adenocarcinoma, ARID1A status, TP53 status, screen-quality strata, growth-rate strata, aneuploidy strata, stemness strata, CRISPR libraries, mutation-burden strata, and KRAS status. 2. KEAP1 loss is robustly associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency. The accepted reverse-direction claim H17/R7 gives +0.796 (0.776 to 0.816), meaning KEAP1-loss lines have raw NFE2L2 dependency scores about 0.80 units higher, i.e. less negative, than KEAP1-intact lines. Validation H17/R13 is +0.801 (validated interval 0.772 to 0.829). This pattern is stable across adenocarcinoma, STK11, TP53, PTEN, KRAS, screen-quality, growth-rate, mutation-burden, aneuploidy, hypoxia, stemness, CRISPR-library, and batch strata. 3. MSI-high status is robustly associated with stronger WRN dependency. H8/R8 is +0.790 (0.760 to 0.819), and independent validation H8/R52 is +0.807 (validated interval 0.759 to 0.855). The association is internally replicated in adenocarcinoma, TP53, KRAS, screen-quality, growth-rate, mutation-burden, aneuploidy, stemness, batch, CRISPR-library, and omics-QC strata. 4. PTEN loss is robustly associated with stronger STAT3 dependency. H14/R15 is +0.267 (0.215 to 0.319), and validation H14/R26 is +0.310 (validated interval 0.231 to 0.388). This is smaller than the SWI/SNF, KEAP1, and MSI effects but is large relative to the STAT3 score distribution and exceeds the practical threshold. It is replicated across lineage, TP53, PIK3CA/PTEN complement, KRAS, mutation-burden, screen-quality, culture, growth-rate, aneuploidy, stemness, batch, CRISPR-library, and IFN strata. 5. TP53 loss is robustly associated with weaker USP7 dependency. H12/R12 is +0.396 (0.325 to 0.467), meaning TP53-loss lines have raw USP7 dependency scores about 0.40 units less negative, i.e. weaker dependency. Validation H12/R65 is +0.395 (validated interval 0.293 to 0.497). The association replicates across adenocarcinoma, MYC, PTEN, KRAS, KEAP1, mutation-burden, screen-quality, growth-rate, aneuploidy, stemness, batch, CRISPR-library, and omics-QC strata. 6. One supported effect modification emerged: IFN-high context appears to amplify the PTEN-loss STAT3 association. The direct high-IFN result H228/R216 is +0.428 (0.326 to 0.529), the low-IFN complement result H230/R218 is +0.207 (0.148 to 0.266), and the formal interaction H231/R219 is +0.221 (0.104 to 0.338). Because the signed interaction is positive under the registered direction of stronger dependency in IFN-high lines relative to the complement, this supports dataset-specific IFN-associated effect modification. Its lower bound is only slightly above the practical 10 percent benchmark, the analysis uses a dichotomized IFN score, and no independent validation of this interaction is available. I therefore accept it as an internal dataset-specific association with limited confidence, not as a validated mechanistic or generalizable finding. Negative findings are substantial. Most simple driver-expected dependencies are unsupported: KRAS mutation is not associated with KRAS or RIT1 dependency; BRAF V600E is not associated with BRAF, KRAS, EGFR, or ERBB2 dependency; EGFR amplification is not associated with accepted EGFR dependency and validation actually contradicts the discovery direction; ERBB2 amplification is not associated with ERBB2 or TMED10 dependency; MDM2 dependency is not explained by TP53 loss or MYC amplification; RPL11, POLR2A, DHX9, KIF18A, TMED10, and RIT1 dependency show little or no association with the tested genomic or culture predictors. MYC amplification does not support broad associations with DHX9, POLR2A, RPL11, USP7, MDM2, WRN, STAT3, NFE2L2, or TMED10 dependency. The tested research markers D, E, and F are negative where tested, apart from unresolved/untested probes. The accepted core estimate H5/R5 is a signed +0.784 (95% interval 0.765 to 0.803), which corresponds to SMARCA4-loss cells having a raw dependency score about 0.78 units lower, i.e. more negative, than SMARCA4-intact cells. KEAP1 loss is robustly associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency. The accepted reverse-direction claim H17/R7 gives +0.796 (0.776 to 0.816), meaning KEAP1-loss lines have raw NFE2L2 dependency scores about 0.80 units higher, i.e. less negative, than KEAP1-intact lines. This pattern is stable across adenocarcinoma, STK11, TP53, PTEN, KRAS, screen-quality, growth-rate, mutation-burden, aneuploidy, hypoxia, stemness, CRISPR-library, and batch strata. 3. MSI-high status is robustly associated with stronger WRN dependency. H8/R8 is +0.790 (0.760 to 0.819), and independent validation H8/R52 is +0.807 (validated interval 0.759 to 0.855). The association is internally replicated in adenocarcinoma, TP53, KRAS, screen-quality, growth-rate, mutation-burden, aneuploidy, stemness, batch, CRISPR-library, and omics-QC strata. 4. PTEN loss is robustly associated with stronger STAT3 dependency. H14/R15 is +0.267 (0.215 to 0.319), and validation H14/R26 is +0.310 (validated interval 0.231 to 0.388). This is smaller than the SWI/SNF, KEAP1, and MSI effects but is large relative to the STAT3 score distribution and exceeds the practical threshold. It is replicated across lineage, TP53, PIK3CA/PTEN complement, KRAS, mutation-burden, screen-quality, culture, growth-rate, aneuploidy, stemness, batch, CRISPR-library, and IFN strata. 5. TP53 loss is robustly associated with weaker USP7 dependency. H12/R12 is +0.396 (0.325 to 0.467), meaning TP53-loss lines have raw USP7 dependency scores about 0.40 units less negative, i.e. weaker dependency. Validation H12/R65 is +0.395 (validated interval 0.293 to 0.497). The association replicates across adenocarcinoma, MYC, PTEN, KRAS, KEAP1, mutation-burden, screen-quality, growth-rate, aneuploidy, stemness, batch, CRISPR-library, and omics-QC strata. 6. One supported effect modification emerged: IFN-high context appears to amplify the PTEN-loss STAT3 association. The direct high-IFN result H228/R216 is +0.428 (0.326 to 0.529), the low-IFN complement result H230/R218 is +0.207 (0.148 to 0.266), and the formal interaction H231/R219 is +0.221 (0.104 to 0.338). Because the signed interaction is positive under the registered direction of stronger dependency in IFN-high lines relative to the complement, this supports dataset-specific IFN-associated effect modification. Its lower bound is only slightly above the practical 10 percent benchmark, the analysis uses a dichotomized IFN score, and no independent validation of this interaction is available. I therefore accept it as an internal dataset-specific association with limited confidence, not as a validated mechanistic or generalizable finding. Negative findings are substantial. Most simple driver-expected dependencies are unsupported: KRAS mutation is not associated with KRAS or RIT1 dependency; BRAF V600E is not associated with BRAF, KRAS, EGFR, or ERBB2 dependency; EGFR amplification is not associated with accepted EGFR dependency and validation actually contradicts the discovery direction; ERBB2 amplification is not associated with ERBB2 or TMED10 dependency; MDM2 dependency is not explained by TP53 loss or MYC amplification; RPL11, POLR2A, DHX9, KIF18A, TMED10, and RIT1 dependency show little or no association with the tested genomic or culture predictors. MYC amplification does not support broad associations with DHX9, POLR2A, RPL11, USP7, MDM2, WRN, STAT3, NFE2L2, or TMED10 dependency. The tested research markers D, E, and F are negative where tested, apart from unresolved/untested probes. Many interaction hypotheses are negative or contradicted: EMT-high modification of PTEN-STAT3 was rejected and independently contradicted, culture modification of MSI-WRN was rejected and validated in the opposite direction, mutation-burden modification of TP53-USP7 was rejected and validated near null, PIK3CA interaction or subgroup effects for STAT3 were not supported, and lineage, culture, screen quality, KRAS, PIK3CA, KEAP1, MYC, and aneuploidy modifiers were largely not supported. H189 remains rejected and closed because validation R193 gave -0.0599 with a validated interval -0.2215 to 0.1018, opposite the registered direction and compatible with no effect. The IFN-high PTEN-STAT3 interaction is the most promising novel finding, but it needs independent confirmation and sensitivity analysis using continuous IFN_gamma_signature rather than a single dichotomization. For all claims, causality cannot be inferred: these are associations measured in a lung-derived, largely adherent-cell-line CRISPR dataset, and measured predictors may be confounded by copy number, mutation burden, culture context, screen quality, or unmodeled interactions. The most informative next analysis would be independent external validation of the IFN-high amplification of PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency using continuous IFN_gamma_signature, prespecified thresholds or spline-based interaction tests, covariate adjustment for PTEN loss, mutation burden, TP53 status, lineage, and screen QC, together with external replication of the five core SMARCA4-SMARCA2, KEAP1-NFE2L2, MSI-high-WRN, PTEN-STAT3, and TP53-USP7 associations."}}

record.narrative:
No assessments are due and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so the scientifically useful next step is internal refinement: test whether the already accepted core dependency associations persist under biologically and technically distinct conditions, and test whether the only accepted effect modification is robust to a higher IFN_gamma threshold. The first two proposals refine the accepted IFN-high amplification of PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency by using a stricter top-quantile-like IFN threshold of ifn_gamma_signature >= 0.6 instead of >= 0.5. The direct contrast tests whether the raw PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency difference remains strongly negative in this high-IFN subset; the interaction tests whether that subset-specific difference remains more negative than in the complement. Both use direction -1, so a positive signed estimate corresponds to stronger, more negative STAT3 dependency in the registered direction.

The next five proposals test the five accepted core associations in a high-ploidy context, ploidy >= 3.0. Ploidy is a distinct genome-state measure from aneuploidy_score, chromosomal instability proxies, mutation burden, screen QC, growth rate, and previously tested interaction contexts. The expectations are persistence of the same signs: SMARCA4 loss remains associated with more negative SMARCA2 dependency; KEAP1 loss remains associated with less negative NFE2L2 dependency; MSI-high remains associated with more negative WRN dependency; PTEN loss remains associated with more negative STAT3 dependency; and TP53 loss remains associated with less negative USP7 dependency. These tests are important because rare-exposure cells could become imprecise or directionally distorted in high-ploidy lines, especially for MSI-high and PTEN loss, but median-like high-ploidy groups should still retain at least 20 exposed and comparator cells for these predictors.

The final five proposals test the same five core associations only in low-serum culture conditions, media_serum_pct == 5.0. Low serum is a culture-context perturbation that can affect proliferation and cell state, and it was not used for the main core-association robustness program. Direct contrasts within the 5% serum subset test whether each association persists when media context is restricted, rather than merely comparing high versus low serum or performing an interaction. Again, the expected signed results are positive under the registered directions if the established associations persist.

All new claims remain dataset-specific associations, not causal claims. Acceptance will require the signed estimate to be in the registered direction, the 95% Welch interval to exclude zero, all comparison cells to satisfy the minimum-n rule, and the magnitude to be scientifically meaningful relative to the practical 10% benchmark or comparable to the already accepted core effects. Near-zero or interval-crossing results should be interpreted as failure to support the registered effect or persistence claim in that dataset, not proof of absence. Interaction results should support context amplification only if the signed interaction is precise and non-null.

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without

Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may

You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment

plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All twelve newly delivered results are signed to the registered hypothesis directions and every comparison cell satisfies the minimum-observation rule. H242 and H243 strengthen the previously identified IFN-high effect modification of the PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency association. At the stricter threshold ifn_gamma_signature >= 0.6, the direct PTEN-loss contrast is +0.452 [0.347, 0.556], indicating substantially stronger STAT3 dependency in the high-IFN PTEN-loss group, while the formal interaction is +0.243 [0.124, 0.362]. Both intervals exclude zero and are above the practical 0.1 magnitude benchmark. I therefore accept both as dataset-specific support for IFN-associated amplification of the PTEN-loss STAT3 association. This remains an internal, threshold-dependent finding: the 0.6 cutoff is close to the earlier 0.5 cutoff, the IFN score is dichotomized, and multiple IFN-related contrasts have now been examined, so confidence is moderate rather than strong and external/generalizable causal claims are not supported. H244-H248 test the five core accepted associations in high-ploidy lines (ploidy >= 3.0). All five persist with signed estimates excluding zero: SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 +0.762 [0.726, 0.798]; KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 +0.802 [0.763, 0.842]; MSI-high/WRN +0.788 [0.732, 0.844]; PTEN-loss/STAT3 +0.243 [0.145, 0.341]; and TP53-loss/USP7 +0.272 [0.127, 0.417]. The magnitudes are either very large or exceed the 0.1 practical benchmark, and the intervals exclude zero. H249-H253 test the same five core associations in low-serum culture (media_serum_pct = 5). All again persist: SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 +0.766 [0.726, 0.805]; KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 +0.788 [0.747, 0.829]; MSI-high/WRN +0.779 [0.711, 0.848]; PTEN-loss/STAT3 +0.214 [0.114, 0.313]; and TP53-loss/USP7 +0.268 [0.108, 0.428]. These are internal stratified robustness tests using overlapping cell-line data, not independent external replications, and should not be overinterpreted as independent confirmations. Nevertheless, they provide consistent evidence that the accepted core associations are not driven by a single ploidy or serum-context subgroup. Because independent validation capacity is exhausted, no validation was requested. These conclusions remain associations in the supplied lung-derived CRISPR dataset, not causal mechanisms or externally generalizable claims.

Independent validation capacity is exhausted. The strongest supported conclusions are dataset-specific CRISPR dependency associations, not causal claims. The evidence supports five internally robust associations: SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, signed effect +0.784 [0.765, 0.803] and validated +0.800 [0.768, 0.832]; KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, signed effect +0.796 [0.776, 0.816] and validated +0.801 [0.772, 0.829]; MSI-high status is associated with stronger WRN dependency, signed effect +0.790 [0.760, 0.819] and validated +0.807 [0.759, 0.855]; PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency, signed effect +0.267 [0.215, 0.319] and validated +0.310 [0.231, 0.388]; and TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency, signed effect +0.396 [0.325, 0.467] and validated +0.395 [0.293, 0.497]. These estimates are signed to the registered hypothesis directions. The only accepted effect modification is IFN-high amplification of the PTEN-loss STAT3 association. Supporting internal evidence includes high-IFN direct effect +0.428 [0.326, 0.529], low-IFN direct effect +0.207 [0.148, 0.266], formal interaction +0.221 [0.104, 0.338], stricter >=0.6 direct effect +0.452 [0.347, 0.556], and stricter >=0.6 interaction +0.243 [0.124, 0.362]. This is meaningful in this dataset but threshold-dependent, internally derived, and not externally validated. Major negative findings are that common driver hypotheses are unsupported: KRAS mutation does not support KRAS or RIT1 dependency, BRAF V600E does not support BRAF/KRAS/EGFR/ERBB2 dependency, EGFR amplification is not accepted and has contradictory validation, ERBB2 amplification does not support ERBB2 or TMED10 dependency, TP53 loss and MYC amplification do not explain MDM2 dependency, and MYC amplification does not show broad associations across tested dependency outcomes. The constructed research markers were negative where tested, and most interaction hypotheses were rejected or contradicted, including EMT modification of PTEN-STAT3, culture modification of MSI-WRN, mutation-burden modification of TP53-USP7, and many lineage, culture, screen-quality, KRAS, PIK3CA, KEAP1, MYC, and genome-instability modifiers. Remaining uncertainty concerns external generalizability, causality, untested deferred predictors, and whether the IFN effect is better modeled continuously rather than by thresholds. The most informative next analysis is an internal IFN threshold-ladder sensitivity analysis, with future external replication ideally using continuous IFN_gamma_signature and covariate-adjusted or spline-based interaction tests. I registered new probes at ifn_gamma_signature >=0.8 and <= -0.5 to test monotonicity and reduce dependence on the previous dichotomization.

record.narrative: No assessments are due and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so the most informative current step is to refine the only accepted effect-modification finding using stricter IFN_gamma thresholds. Previously, PTEN loss was accepted as associated with stronger STAT3 dependency overall, and IFN-high amplification of that association was accepted at thresholds >=0.5 and >=0.6. Active but not yet analyzed probes test ifn_gamma_signature >=0.8 direct and interaction, plus ifn_gamma_signature <=-0.5 direct. I do not repeat those active claims. Instead, I register a threshold ladder with high IFN >=1.0 and low IFN <=-0.75 and <=-1.0. The high-IFN direct contrasts test whether the PTEN-loss STAT3-dependency association becomes stronger in increasingly IFN-selected lines. The high-IFN interaction contrasts test whether that subset difference is more negative than in the IFN-lower/mid complement; under direction -1, a positive signed estimate supports amplification. The low-IFN direct contrasts test whether the PTEN-loss association persists in very low IFN contexts. The low-IFN interaction contrasts use direction +1 because low IFN attenuation predicts a less negative PTEN-loss contrast than the non-low IFN complement, giving a positive raw interaction. These are dataset-specific association tests, not causal or generalizable claims. If an extreme threshold has fewer than 20 observations in any cell, it should be treated as not assessable rather than as evidence against the association. If intervals cross zero, interpret as lack of support in this dataset for that threshold-specific claim.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

record.narrative: No assessments are due, and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so I request only new or still-untested discovery analyses that can add information from the supplied dataset. I select seven already registered but untested IFN threshold-ladder refinements, H254-H260, rather than rerunning claims that already have evidence. Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative:
No independent validation capacity remains, and no claim is listed in assessments_due; no new validation response deadline is present. I therefore keep the accepted claim set essentially unchanged, but close the two very-low IFN probes H261/H262 as investigation-only unresolved because the <= -1 stratum is sparse, likely invalid for minimum cell sizes, and redundant with the <= -0.75 contrasts.

The strongest supported findings are five internally robust, signed associations with meaningful absolute magnitudes relative to the 10% threshold. SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency: discovery +0.784 [0.765, 0.803] R5 and independent validation +0.800 [0.768, 0.832] R39. KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency: signed discovery +0.796 [0.776, 0.816] R7 and validation +0.801 [0.772, 0.829] R13. MSI-high status is associated with stronger WRN dependency: +0.790 [0.760, 0.819] R8 and validation +0.807 [0.759, 0.855] R52. PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency: +0.267 [0.215, 0.319] R15 and validation +0.310 [0.231, 0.388] R26. TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency: +0.396 [0.325, 0.467] R12 and validation +0.395 [0.293, 0.497] R65. These are dataset-specific associations, not causal claims; the accepted subgroup and eligibility analyses are additional internal sensitivity checks, not external replication.

The only supported effect modification is high IFN amplification of the PTEN-loss/STAT3-dependency association. Direct PTEN-loss contrasts are accepted in IFN-high strata: >=0.5 +0.428 [0.326, 0.529] R216, >=0.6 +0.452 [0.347, 0.556] R230, and >=0.8 +0.436 [0.308, 0.565] R242. Formal interactions are also accepted at >=0.5 +0.221 [0.104, 0.338] R219, >=0.6 +0.243 [0.124, 0.362] R231, and >=0.8 +0.200 [0.060, 0.339] R243. At the extreme threshold >=1.0, the direct contrast persists +0.342 [0.176, 0.508] R245, but the interaction is not supported +0.083 [-0.091, 0.257] R246. Low IFN direct contrasts persist, e.g. <= -0.5 +0.138 [0.041, 0.235] R244 and <= -0.75 +0.162 [0.037, 0.286] R247, but the corresponding low IFN interaction is not supported at <= -0.75 +0.127 [-0.010, 0.264] R248. Thus IFN modification appears specific to moderate/high thresholds (0.5, 0.6, and 0.8), is threshold dependent, and remains unvalidated externally.

Major negative findings are scientifically informative. KRAS mutation does not support KRAS, RIT1, BRAF, or STAT3 dependency hypotheses. BRAF V600E does not support BRAF, KRAS, EGFR, ERBB2, or RIT1 dependency hypotheses. EGFR amplification is rejected and has contradictory validation; ERBB2 amplification does not support ERBB2 or TMED10 dependency. TP53 loss explains USP7 dependency but not MDM2, STAT3, SMARCA2, WRN, or RPL11 dependencies. MYC amplification shows no broad association across the tested dependency outcomes. The constructed research markers D/E/F were null where tested, including SMARCA2 with markers E/F, WRN with D, NFE2L2 with D, and STAT3 with F. Most interaction hypotheses were rejected, including lineage, culture, screen quality, PIK3CA, KEAP1, MYC, EMT, mutation-burden, and genome-instability modifiers; only PTEN-loss/STAT3 modification by high IFN survived.

Remaining uncertainty is substantial. The run has exhausted independent validation capacity, and many accepted direct effects have only validation for the five core markers. IFN dichotomization and threshold selection could inflate specificity; external generalizability and causal interpretation are not established. Some deferred comparisons remain untested, and sparse strata such as the lowest IFN tail or extreme MSI-high subgroups have limited power. The most informative next internal analyses are the four proposed interaction sensitivity tests: whether IFN-high context also modifies the SMARCA4/SMARCA2, MSI-high/WRN, or TP53/USP7 associations, and whether MYC amplification modifies the KEAP1/NFE2L2 association. Null results would support the view that IFN effect modification is specific to PTEN-loss/STAT3 in this dataset; non-null interactions would indicate broader contextual dependency. Minimum-cell-size validity must be checked before interpreting these new interaction estimates. Future external work should use continuous IFN modeling with covariate adjustment or spline-based interaction tests rather than post-hoc thresholded subsets.

Iteration 21/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

ARID1A loss showed no overall SMARCA2 association in H20, but a SMARCA4-wildtype context asks whether any ARID1A effect is masked by strong SMARCA4-loss effects; a negative result would support SMARCA4 specificity in this dataset. WRN/MSI-high and BRCA2-loss hypotheses are split to see whether MSI-high association persists in BRCA2-wildtype lines and whether BRCA2-loss association is independently visible among MSI-negative lines. Reversing the MDM2/TP53 contrast tests whether TP53-wildtype lines have stronger MDM2 dependency, a more direct p53-MDM2 feedback hypothesis than the previously rejected TP53-loss direction. Second, I test whether the accepted high-IFN amplification of PTEN-loss/STAT3 dependency is specific to PTEN/STAT3 by asking whether high IFN also modifies or is compatible with the other accepted core effects. Direct high-IFN contrasts for SMARCA2/SMARCA4-loss, NFE2L2/KEAP1-loss, and USP7/TP53-loss test persistence of the main effects in an IFN-selected subgroup; these are interpretive complements to active high-IFN interaction tests and should not be read as effect-modification claims unless interactions are also non-null. A KEAP1/NFE2L2 high-IFN interaction specifically tests whether IFN also modifies the KEAP1 attenuation hypothesis; a null interaction would support IFN specificity for PTEN/STAT3, while a non-null result would indicate broader contextual modification. Third, I refine the STAT3 IFN threshold ladder at IFN_gamma_signature >=0.7, between the accepted >=0.6 and >=0.8 findings, and add a lower IFN >=0.4 WRN interaction probe to improve cell counts for the rare MSI-high exposure. Expected directions are stated in the proposal fields: SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 stronger and MSI-high/WRN stronger are negative raw contrasts; KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 weaker and TP53-loss/USP7 weaker are positive raw contrasts. Interaction claims are signed to the expected direction of modification: negative for amplification of a negative main effect and positive for amplification of a positive main effect. Many IFN or MSI strata are sparse; any comparison failing the 20-observation-per-cell rule should be treated as not assessable rather than as negative evidence. record.narrative: No assessments are due and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so this analyze step requests only new discovery analyses from the supplied dataset. I select 12 registered but still untested active claims. The selection prioritizes two questions: (1) whether the previously supported high-interferon effect modification is specific to the PTEN-loss/STAT3 association, and (2) whether accepted core associations remain specific in more informative genetic contexts. For interferon specificity, I run direct high-IFN contrasts for the other core effects (H272-H274) and formal high-IFN interaction tests for SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2 (H263), MSI-high/WRN (H264), TP53 loss/USP7 (H265), and KEAP1 loss/NFE2L2 (H271). I also include H275, the lower IFN threshold >=0.4 interaction for MSI-high/WRN, because MSI-high is rare and the lower threshold may provide more usable cell counts. H266 tests whether MYC amplification modifies the KEAP1 loss/NFE2L2 association, providing a non-IFN modifier sensitivity check. For genetic specificity, H267 asks whether ARID1A loss is associated with SMARCA2 dependency among SMARCA4-wildtype lines, addressing whether the overall ARID1A null might mask a context-specific effect. H268 and H269 separate the WRN hypotheses into BRCA2-wildtype and MSI-negative contexts, respectively, to test whether MSI-high/WRN persists when BRCA2 loss is absent and whether BRCA2 loss has an independent association in MSS lines. For all signed analyses, a positive estimate with an interval excluding zero supports the registered direction; intervals crossing zero or small point estimates will be treated as insufficient support, especially in sparse strata. Any comparison failing the minimum cell-size rule will be treated as non-assessable rather than as null evidence. All interpretations remain dataset-specific associations, not causal claims or generalizable biological claims.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.
