record.narrative: All twelve newly delivered discovery analyses have valid minimum cell counts, and the estimates are interpreted as already signed to the registered hypothesis directions. The IFN specificity probes are scientifically informative: the formal high-IFN interaction tests for SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2 (H263, R254: -0.027 [-0.071,0.016]), MSI-high/WRN (H264, R255: +0.024 [-0.036,0.084]), TP53 loss/USP7 (H265, R256: -0.044 [-0.218,0.130]), and KEAP1 loss/NFE2L2 (H271, R257: -0.006 [-0.052,0.040]) are all imprecise or near-null and cross the no-effect region. Their point estimates are far below the practical 10% benchmark. I therefore reject these interaction claims as unsupported in this dataset. Together with the accepted high-IFN PTEN-loss/STAT3 interactions, these nulls support the narrower dataset-specific conclusion that IFN_gamma_signature effect modification is specific to the PTEN-loss/STAT3 association among the tested core effects. The lower-threshold IFN>=0.4 MSI-high/WRN interaction (H275, R261: +0.015 [-0.044,0.075]) is also null despite better cell counts, further weakening any broad WRN-MSI/IFN modification hypothesis. The direct effects in IFN-high strata remain large and robust: KEAP1 loss/NFE2L2 (H272, R258: +0.792 [0.752,0.831]), TP53 loss/USP7 (H273, R259: +0.363 [0.208,0.518]), and SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2 (H274, R260: +0.764 [0.727,0.801]). All exclude zero and exceed the practical magnitude threshold, so I accept them as internal evidence that the core associations persist in IFN-high subsets. These are not new effect-modification claims. The MYC amplification interaction on KEAP1 loss/NFE2L2 (H266, R262: -0.008 [-0.072,0.057]) is null, supporting absence of MYC amplification as a modifier of that association. The genetic-context tests are also decisive: ARID1A loss among SMARCA4-wildtype lines has no meaningful SMARCA2 association (H267, R263: -0.003 [-0.025,0.019]), supporting SMARCA4-specificity rather than broad PBAF/ARID1A-related synthetic lethality in this dataset. MSI-high remains strongly associated with WRN dependency among BRCA2-wildtype lines (H268, R264: +0.794 [0.764,0.825]), whereas BRCA2 loss has no association among MSI-negative lines (H269, R265: +0.001 [-0.031,0.032]). This separates the WRN finding from BRCA2-loss synthetic-lethal hypotheses and supports MSI-high as the relevant marker in this dataset. Overall, the new evidence strengthens the accepted core associations and the IFN-specific PTEN/STAT3 modifier, while rejecting the broader IFN, MYC, ARID1A, and BRCA2 modification hypotheses. These remain associations in the supplied dataset only; multiple thresholded IFN tests and dichotomization limit generalizability and causal interpretation. Independent validation capacity is exhausted, so no validation request is made.

Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative: No new validation result or response deadline is listed for this synthesis, and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so I consolidate the existing evidence and make no validation request. The strongest, internally robust, signed associations in the supplied dataset are five marker-to-dependency relationships whose magnitudes exceed the 10% practical benchmark and are internally consistent across many eligibility strata. First, SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency: signed discovery +0.784 [0.765, 0.803] on R5 and independent validation +0.800 [0.768, 0.832] on R39. Second, KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency: signed discovery +0.796 [0.776, 0.816] on R7 and validation +0.801 [0.772, 0.829] on R13. Third, MSI-high status is associated with stronger WRN dependency: signed discovery +0.790 [0.760, 0.819] on R8 and validation +0.807 [0.759, 0.855] on R52. Fourth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency: signed discovery +0.267 [0.215, 0.319] on R15 and validation +0.310 [0.231, 0.388] on R26. Fifth, TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency: signed discovery +0.396 [0.325, 0.467] on R12 and validation +0.395 [0.293, 0.497] on R65. These are dataset-specific associations, not causal or external biological claims. The only supported effect modification is high interferon context amplifying the PTEN-loss STAT3-dependency association. Direct PTEN-loss contrasts persist in IFN-high strata: IFN >= 0.5 signed +0.428 [0.326, 0.529] on R216, IFN >= 0.6 +0.452 [0.347, 0.556] on R230, and IFN >= 0.8 +0.436 [0.308, 0.565] on R242. Formal interactions are supported at the same moderate-to-high thresholds: +0.221 [0.104, 0.338] on R219, +0.243 [0.124, 0.362] on R231, and +0.200 [0.060, 0.339] on R243. By contrast, the extreme IFN >= 1.0 interaction is unsupported at +0.083 [-0.091, 0.257] on R246, and the low-IFN tail interaction at IFN <= -0.75 is unsupported at +0.127 [-0.010, 0.264] on R248. The low-IFN direct contrasts remain positive but smaller, for example +0.138 [0.041, 0.235] on R244 and +0.162 [0.037, 0.286] on R247. Thus, if this dataset is summarized as a whole, IFN appears to amplify PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency at thresholds around 0.5 to 0.8, while the modification is not robust at the extreme high tail and is not supported as a low-tail interaction. Importantly, this effect modification is specific to PTEN-loss STAT3 among the tested core effects: high-IFN interaction tests for SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2, MSI-high WRN, TP53-loss USP7, and KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 are all null or imprecise, R254 -0.027 [-0.071, 0.016], R255 +0.024 [-0.036, 0.084], R256 -0.044 [-0.218, 0.130], and R257 -0.006 [-0.052, 0.040]. The lower-threshold WRN IFN interaction is also null at +0.015 [-0.044, 0.075] on R261. MYC amplification does not modify KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 dependency, R262 -0.008 [-0.072, 0.057]. The new context tests also strengthen marker specificity: ARID1A loss among SMARCA4-wildtype lines is null for SMARCA2, R263 -0.003 [-0.025, 0.019], supporting SMARCA4-specific association rather than a broad ARID1A synthetic-lethal effect. MSI-high remains strongly associated with WRN dependency among BRCA2-wildtype lines, R264 +0.794 [0.764, 0.825], while BRCA2 loss among MSI-negative lines is null, R265 +0.001 [-0.031, 0.032], supporting MSI-high rather than BRCA2-loss as the relevant marker in this dataset. Major negative findings are scientifically useful. KRAS mutation does not support KRAS, RIT1, BRAF, or STAT3 dependency hypotheses; BRAF V600E does not support BRAF, KRAS, EGFR, ERBB2, or RIT1 dependency hypotheses; EGFR amplification is rejected and has discordant discovery/validation behavior on R3 and R119; ERBB2 amplification does not support ERBB2 or TMED10 dependency hypotheses. TP53 loss explains USP7 dependency but not MDM2, STAT3, SMARCA2, WRN, or RPL11 dependencies. MYC amplification shows no broad association across the tested dependency outcomes. The constructed research markers D/E/F are null where tested. Most interaction hypotheses are rejected, including lineage, culture, screen quality, PIK3CA, KEAP1, MYC, EMT, mutation-burden, ploidy, IFN for non-STAT3 outcomes, and BRCA2-specificity tests. Remaining uncertainty is substantial. The accepted findings are associations in this supplied dataset only; causal mechanisms are not established. Independent validation is limited mostly to the core marker outcomes, and IFN thresholding was explored across multiple cutoffs, so the IFN-specific PTEN/STAT3 modification could be sensitive to post-hoc dichotomization. Some deferred or active comparisons remain untested, including the IFN >= 0.7 direct and interaction probes H276 and H277. The most informative next analysis would be to evaluate IFN >= 0.7 if cell-size rules are met and, ideally, replace thresholded IFN analyses with continuous or spline-based IFN modeling with covariate adjustment for PTEN-loss STAT3 interaction. If that does not change the conclusion, the final scientific position is: five robust dataset-specific marker-dependency associations, and one supported threshold-dependent effect modifier, high IFN amplification of PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency, with broad support for nullity of other tested driver, marker, and interaction hypotheses.

Iteration 22/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: All twelve new discovery results have valid Welch diagnostics and satisfy the minimum cell-size rule, and estimates are interpreted as already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. H276 provides strong internal evidence that the PTEN-loss STAT3-dependency association persists in the IFN_gamma_signature >= 0.7 stratum: signed +0.447, 95% CI 0.335 to 0.559, well above the practical 0.10 benchmark. H277 formally supports effect modification in the same stratum: interaction +0.222, 95% CI 0.097 to 0.347. This fills the previously untested 0.7 threshold and is consistent with the accepted IFN >= 0.5, >= 0.6, and >= 0.8 interactions, while the extreme IFN >= 1.0 interaction remains unsupported. Because these IFN thresholds are overlapping and thresholded, the accepted IFN modification should remain a cautious dataset-specific association rather than a precise mechanistic threshold claim, but the pattern supports moderate-high IFN contexts amplifying PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency. H278-H282 robustly replicate the five core marker-dependency associations in the higher-Cas9-activity stratum: SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency +0.788, MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency +0.776, PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency +0.257, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency +0.800, and TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency +0.390; all CIs exclude zero. These are not new independent causal effects, but they strengthen technical plausibility that the associations are not obviously artifacts of poor editing in this dataset. H283 accepts a direct PTEN-loss STAT3 association in hypoxia >= 0.5: +0.251, CI 0.149 to 0.352. However, H284 rejects hypoxia as an amplifier of the STAT3 association: interaction -0.0235, CI -0.141 to 0.094. H285 rejects a hypoxia interaction for KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 dependency: -0.0225, CI -0.070 to 0.025. H286 and H287 reject high MYC mRNA abundance as an interaction context for KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 (+0.0297, CI -0.028 to 0.087) and SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 (+0.0188, CI -0.039 to 0.076), both near zero and below the practical benchmark. I accept the direct stratum results as internal robustness evidence and reject the interaction/modifier hypotheses as unsupported. No validation request is made because independent validation capacity is exhausted. All conclusions remain associations in the supplied dataset, not causal or generalizable biological claims.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link

plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

record.narrative: No new independent validation result or response deadline is listed, and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so this synthesis consolidates the currently available discovery and validation evidence without changing validation status. The controller-maintained accepted set remains appropriate because no assessments_due were returned and no validation response deadline requires reassessment. The scientific conclusions are associations in this supplied dataset only; they are not causal claims and do not establish generalizability to other cell-line collections, screens, or populations. The strongest supported findings are five marker-dependency associations whose magnitudes exceed the practical 0.10 benchmark and are internally consistent across many strata. First, SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency: accepted signed discovery estimate +0.784 on R5, 95% CI 0.765 to 0.803, with independent validation +0.800 on R39, 95% CI 0.768 to 0.832. Second, KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency: signed discovery +0.796 on R7, CI 0.776 to 0.816, and independent validation +0.801 on R13, CI 0.772 to 0.829. Third, MSI-high status is associated with stronger WRN dependency: signed discovery +0.790 on R8, CI 0.760 to 0.819, with independent validation +0.807 on R52, CI 0.759 to 0.855. Fourth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency: signed discovery +0.267 on R15, CI 0.215 to 0.319, and independent validation +0.310 on R26, CI 0.231 to 0.388. Fifth, TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency: signed discovery +0.396 on R12, CI 0.325 to 0.467, and independent validation +0.395 on R65, CI 0.293 to 0.497. The new iteration strengthens technical plausibility of the core set in a higher-Cas9-activity stratum: SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 effect +0.788 on R268, MSI-high WRN effect +0.776 on R269, PTEN-loss STAT3 effect +0.257 on R270, KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 effect +0.800 on R271, and TP53-loss USP7 effect +0.390 on R272. These high-Cas9 stratum results are not additional independent causal replication, but they reduce the concern that the core associations are simple artifacts of weak editing in this dataset. The only supported effect modification remains high interferon context amplifying PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency. Direct PTEN-loss contrasts persist and are large in moderate-to-high IFN strata: IFN >= 0.5 +0.428 on R216, IFN >= 0.6 +0.452 on R230, IFN >= 0.7 +0.447 on R266, and IFN >= 0.8 +0.436 on R242. Formal interactions are supported at those same moderate-to-high thresholds: +0.221 on R219, +0.243 on R231, +0.222 on R267, and +0.200 on R243. By contrast, the extreme IFN >= 1.0 interaction is unsupported at +0.083 on R246, and the low-IFN tail interaction is unsupported at +0.127 on R248. Direct PTEN-loss effects remain positive but smaller in low-IFN contexts, for example +0.138 on R244 and +0.162 on R247. Thus, if summarized using thresholds, this dataset supports amplification of PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency around IFN thresholds of approximately 0.5 to 0.8, while it does not support robust modification at the extreme high tail or at the tested low tail. The IFN modification is also specific among the tested core effects: interactions for SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 R254, MSI-high WRN R255 and R261, TP53-loss USP7 R256, and KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 R257 are null or imprecise. Marker specificity is further supported by ARID1A loss being null for SMARCA2 among SMARCA4-wildtype lines on R263, and BRCA2 loss being null for WRN among MSI-negative lines on R265. Major negative findings are scientifically useful. Driver/amplification hypotheses are largely unsupported: KRAS mutation does not support KRAS, RIT1, BRAF, or STAT3 dependency hypotheses; BRAF V600E does not support BRAF, KRAS, EGFR, ERBB2, or RIT1 dependency hypotheses; EGFR amplification is rejected, with discordant behavior between discovery R3 and validation R119; ERBB2 amplification does not support ERBB2 or TMED10 dependency hypotheses. TP53 loss supports USP7 but not MDM2, STAT3, SMARCA2, WRN, or RPL11 dependencies. MYC DNA amplification shows no broad meaningful association across tested dependencies. Most interaction hypotheses are rejected, including lineage subtype, culture type, PIK3CA, KEAP1, MYC amplification, EMT, mutation-burden, ploidy, screen quality, and IFN modification of outcomes other than PTEN-loss STAT3. The constructed research markers D, E, and F are null where tested. The new context tests also clarify boundaries: high hypoxia does not modify PTEN-loss STAT3 interaction R274 or KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 interaction R275, although a direct PTEN-loss STAT3 association persists in hypoxia R273; high MYC mRNA abundance does not modify KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 R276 or SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 R277. Remaining uncertainty is substantial. record.narrative: No assessments are due and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so this explore step registers additional discovery comparisons from the supplied dataset. The existing active registered claims already target the lower-Cas9 direct effects for the five core marker-dependency associations and a high-Cas9 IFN direct plus interaction test for PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency. The new proposals add focused refinements in two remaining areas. First, IFN_gamma_signature modification of PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency has been supported across overlapping thresholds >=0.5, >=0.6, >=0.7, and >=0.8, but the extreme >=1.0 interaction was unsupported and the lower boundary below 0.5 was not tested. The proposed >=0.9 direct and interaction tests bracket the supported 0.8 threshold against the unsupported 1.0 threshold, and the proposed >=0.4 tests probe whether modification begins below 0.5. Because these are dichotomized threshold tests on overlapping subsets, I expect uncertainty and treat them as mapping boundary robustness, not as continuous IFN modeling. Second, to test whether low measured Cas9 activity could create spurious marker associations, I registered ARID1A loss versus SMARCA2 dependency among SMARCA4-wildtype lines within the lower Cas9 stratum. Prior full-population ARID1A loss was null for SMARCA2, and this is a marker-specificity context test. Across all proposals, estimates and intervals are interpreted as already signed to the registered direction. I will accept only if the interval excludes zero and the effect is scientifically meaningful, using the established practical benchmark of roughly 0.10 dependency-score units. Comparisons failing the 20-observation-per-cell requirement will be treated as non-assessable, not as negative evidence. All conclusions remain associations in this dataset, not causal mechanisms or generalizable claims.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation

initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.

This fills the previously untested 0.7 threshold and is consistent with the accepted IFN >= 0.5, >= 0.6, and >= 0.8 interactions, while the extreme IFN >= 1.0 interaction remains unsupported. Because these IFN thresholds are overlapping and thresholded, the accepted IFN modification should remain a cautious dataset-specific association rather than a precise mechanistic threshold claim, but the pattern supports moderate-high IFN contexts amplifying PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency. H278-H282 robustly replicate the five core marker-dependency associations in the higher-Cas9-activity stratum: SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency +0.788, MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency +0.776, PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency +0.257, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency +0.800, and TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency +0.390; all CIs exclude zero. These are not new independent causal effects, but they strengthen technical plausibility that the associations are not obviously artifacts of poor editing in this dataset. Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction

Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are

You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

Second, KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency: signed discovery +0.796 on R7, CI 0.776 to 0.816, and independent validation +0.801 on R13, CI 0.772 to 0.829. Third, MSI-high status is associated with stronger WRN dependency: signed discovery +0.790 on R8, CI 0.760 to 0.819, with independent validation +0.807 on R52, CI 0.759 to 0.855. Fourth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency: signed discovery +0.267 on R15, CI 0.215 to 0.319, and independent validation +0.310 on R26, CI 0.231 to 0.388. Fifth, TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency: signed discovery +0.396 on R12, CI 0.325 to 0.467, and independent validation +0.395 on R65, CI 0.293 to 0.497. The new iteration strengthens technical plausibility of the core set in a higher-Cas9-activity stratum: SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 effect +0.788 on R268, MSI-high WRN effect +0.776 on R269, PTEN-loss STAT3 effect +0.257 on R270, KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 effect +0.800 on R271, and TP53-loss USP7 effect +0.390 on R272. These high-Cas9 stratum results are not additional independent causal replication, but they reduce the concern that the core associations are simple artifacts of weak editing in this dataset. The only supported effect modification remains high interferon context amplifying PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency. Direct PTEN-loss contrasts persist and are large in moderate-to-high IFN strata: IFN >= 0.5 +0.428 on R216, IFN >= 0.6 +0.452 on R230, IFN >= 0.7 +0.447 on R266, and IFN >= 0.8 +0.436 on R242. Formal interactions are supported at those same moderate-to-high thresholds: +0.221 on R219, +0.243 on R231, +0.222 on R267, and +0.200 on R243. By contrast, the extreme IFN >= 1.0 interaction is unsupported at +0.083 on R246, and the low-IFN tail interaction is unsupported at +0.127 on R248. Direct PTEN-loss effects remain positive but smaller in low-IFN contexts, for example +0.138 on R244 and +0.162 on R247. Thus, if summarized using thresholds, this dataset supports amplification of PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency around IFN thresholds of approximately 0.5 to 0.8, while it does not support robust modification at the extreme high tail or at the tested low tail. The IFN modification is also specific among the tested core effects: interactions for SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 R254, MSI-high WRN R255 and R261, TP53-loss USP7 R256, and KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 R257 are null or imprecise. Marker specificity is further supported by ARID1A loss being null for SMARCA2 among SMARCA4-wildtype lines on R263, and BRCA2 loss being null for WRN among MSI-negative lines on R265. Major negative findings are scientifically useful. Driver/amplification hypotheses are largely unsupported: KRAS mutation does not support KRAS, RIT1, BRAF, or STAT3 dependency hypotheses; BRAF V600E does not support BRAF, KRAS, EGFR, ERBB2, or RIT1 dependency hypotheses; EGFR amplification is rejected, with discordant behavior between discovery R3 and validation R119; ERBB2 amplification does not support ERBB2 or TMED10 dependency hypotheses. TP53 loss supports USP7 but not MDM2, STAT3, SMARCA2, WRN, or RPL11 dependencies. MYC DNA amplification shows no broad meaningful association across tested dependencies. Most interaction hypotheses are rejected, including lineage subtype, culture type, PIK3CA, KEAP1, MYC amplification, EMT, mutation-burden, ploidy, screen quality, and IFN modification of outcomes other than PTEN-loss STAT3. The constructed research markers D, E, and F are null where tested. The new context tests also clarify boundaries: high hypoxia does not modify PTEN-loss STAT3 interaction R274 or KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 interaction R275, although a direct PTEN-loss STAT3 association persists in hypoxia R273; high MYC mRNA abundance does not modify KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 R276 or SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 R277. Remaining uncertainty is substantial. First, causal direction is unknown: SMARCA4 loss, KEAP1 loss, MSI-high, PTEN loss, TP53 loss, and IFN contexts are associated with dependency-score differences, but the data do not prove that the marker causes the dependency change or that IFN causes amplification. Second, the IFN conclusion relies on repeated dichotomized thresholds and overlapping subsets; the robust supported range appears to be 0.5 to 0.8, while 1.0 is unsupported, so a continuous or spline model with covariate adjustment would be the most scientifically informative way to avoid threshold artifacts. Third, lower Cas9 activity was not tested. The high-Cas9 acceptances show persistence under favorable editing, but it is still important to test whether the five core associations attenuate, persist, or disappear in a lower-Cas9 stratum. Fourth, the IFN modification has not been tested jointly within high Cas9, which could determine whether the supported amplification is robust across editing-quality context. The most informative next analyses are therefore the registered lower-Cas9 direct probes for the five core associations, plus direct and interaction tests of PTEN-loss STAT3 high-IFN effect modification restricted to high Cas9. If lower-Cas9 effects persist, technical robustness would be stronger; if they attenuate, editing context may matter for the magnitude of the associations. If high-Cas9 IFN interaction persists, the IFN result becomes less likely to be an artifact of editing-quality imbalance, though threshold sensitivity and generalizability would remain unresolved."}}

record.narrative: All twelve new discovery comparisons are valid by Welch diagnostics and satisfy the minimum cell-size rule; estimates and intervals are interpreted as already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. H288-H292 support the five core marker-dependency associations within the lower-Cas9-activity stratum: SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 dependency +0.754, KEAP1-loss weaker NFE2L2 dependency +0.799, MSI-high WRN dependency +0.798, PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency +0.372, and TP53-loss weaker USP7 dependency +0.315, each with intervals excluding zero and magnitudes above the practical 0.10 dependency-score-unit benchmark. This is internally consistent with the full-population and higher-Cas9 stratum results, reducing the concern that the core associations are artifacts of poor editing in this dataset, but it is still same-dataset evidence and not independent causal replication. H293-H294 accept a high-Cas9 high-IFN extension of the PTEN-loss STAT3 association: direct effect +0.512 and interaction +0.330. These are supported but use relatively small exposed cells, so they should remain cautious dataset-specific associations. H295 accepts a direct PTEN-loss STAT3 association at IFN>=0.9, but H296 rejects the corresponding interaction because the interval crosses zero; a strong direct association alone does not establish IFN amplification. H297-H298 accept direct and interaction effects at IFN>=0.4, extending the supported amplification pattern to the lower boundary near 0.4. The threshold pattern is therefore supported at approximately IFN>=0.4 through 0.8, unsupported at IFN>=0.9 and IFN>=1.0, with low-tail modification also unsupported. Because these IFN thresholds are overlapping, dichotomized, and selected after many comparisons, this should be interpreted as a rough context mapping rather than a precise mechanistic threshold. H299 rejects ARID1A loss as a meaningful SMARCA2-dependency effect among SMARCA4-wildtype lower-Cas9 lines; the interval is centered near zero and excludes meaningful magnitudes. This supports specificity of the SMARCA4 association but does not prove absence. No validation request is possible because independent validation capacity is exhausted. All conclusions remain associations in the supplied dataset, with residual uncertainty from multiplicity, overlapping threshold tests, small high-stratum cells, potential confounding by correlated molecular or screen features, and lack of causal or generalizable evidence.

First, SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency: accepted signed discovery estimate +0.784 on R5, 95% CI 0.765 to 0.803, with independent validation +0.800 on R39, 95% CI 0.768 to 0.832. Third, MSI-high status is associated with stronger WRN dependency: signed discovery +0.790 on R8, CI 0.760 to 0.819, with independent validation +0.807 on R52, CI 0.759 to 0.855. Fourth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency: signed discovery +0.267 on R15, CI 0.215 to 0.319, and independent validation +0.310 on R26, CI 0.231 to 0.388. Fifth, TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency: signed discovery +0.396 on R12, CI 0.325 to 0.467, and independent validation +0.395 on R65, CI 0.293 to 0.497. The new iteration strengthens technical plausibility of the core set in a higher-Cas9-activity stratum: SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 effect +0.788 on R268, MSI-high WRN effect +0.776 on R269, PTEN-loss STAT3 effect +0.257 on R270, KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 effect +0.800 on R271, and TP53-loss USP7 effect +0.390 on R272. These high-Cas9 stratum results are not additional independent causal replication, but they reduce the concern that the core associations are simple artifacts of weak editing in this dataset. The only supported effect modification remains high interferon context amplifying PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency. Direct PTEN-loss contrasts persist and are large in moderate-to-high IFN strata: IFN >= 0.5 +0.428 on R216, IFN >= 0.6 +0.452 on R230, IFN >= 0.7 +0.447 on R266, and IFN >= 0.8 +0.436 on R242. By contrast, the extreme IFN >= 1.0 interaction is unsupported at +0.083 on R246, and the low-IFN tail interaction is unsupported at +0.127 on R248. Direct PTEN-loss effects remain positive but smaller in low-IFN contexts, for example +0.138 on R244 and +0.162 on R247. Thus, if summarized using thresholds, this dataset supports amplification of PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency around IFN thresholds of approximately 0.5 to 0.8, while it does not support robust modification at the extreme high tail or at the tested low tail. The IFN modification is also specific among the tested core effects: interactions for SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 R254, MSI-high WRN R255 and R261, TP53-loss USP7 R256, and KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 R257 are null or imprecise. Marker specificity is further supported by ARID1A loss being null for SMARCA2 among SMARCA4-wildtype lines on R263, and BRCA2 loss being null for WRN among MSI-negative lines on R265. Major negative findings are scientifically useful. results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

expectation

record.narrative: No assessments are due, and independent validation capacity remains exhausted, so this step registers additional discovery comparisons and defers already accepted active context claims to free analysis attention. The main supported dataset-specific associations remain the five core marker-dependency links; the most unresolved question is whether the PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency effect is robustly amplified by interferon context across editing-quality strata and whether similar IFN modification is specific to STAT3 among the core outcomes. The new proposals therefore focus on three priorities. First, they map the IFN boundary: direct PTEN-loss STAT3 association in IFN<=0.399 tests whether the association begins to attenuate below the supported approximate 0.4 threshold, while the high-Cas9 IFN>=0.4 interaction tests whether the supported amplification pattern extends to lower IFN threshold within higher Cas9 activity. Second, they test context and marker specificity: direct PTEN-loss STAT3 in low hypoxia checks whether the PTEN-loss STAT3 effect is IFN-specific or more generally context-dependent, and lower-Cas9 IFN interactions for TP53-loss USP7 and SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 test whether IFN modification is specific to PTEN-loss STAT3. High-Cas9 ARID1A testing among SMARCA4-wildtype lines is a marker-specificity control. Third, media-serum robustness in the larger 10% serum stratum tests whether the strongest core associations persist in a common culture condition. For all signed estimates, acceptance requires an interval excluding zero and a scientifically meaningful magnitude, with roughly 0.10 dependency-score units as the practical benchmark. Null intervals near zero will be treated as non-support for the registered effect, not proof of absence. All conclusions remain associations in this supplied dataset, not causal or generalizable claims.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.

and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released

deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are

only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: No new validation was delivered at this synthesis and validation.remaining_new_requests=0, so no new independent interval changes a claim and no response deadline is active. I therefore leave the controller-maintained accepted set unchanged and consolidate the evidence already available in this supplied dataset. All conclusions are associations in these 2000 lung-derived lines, not causal claims and not generalizable to other screens, platforms, or populations. Because CRISPR dependency scores are signed continuous scores rather than relative clinical outcomes, I used the practical benchmark carried through this run, roughly 0.10 dependency-score unit, together with interval precision, to judge scientific meaningfulness. The five strongest supported findings are SMARCA4-loss association with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, KEAP1-loss association with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, MSI-high association with stronger WRN dependency, PTEN-loss association with stronger STAT3 dependency, and TP53-loss association with weaker USP7 dependency. First, SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency: H5/R5 signed +0.784 (95% CI 0.765 to 0.803), with independent validation R39 +0.800 (95% CI 0.768 to 0.832). This is robust across many context strata, including high Cas9 activity R268 +0.788, lower Cas9 activity R278 +0.754, high IFN R260, and 10% serum R300 +0.799. Marker specificity is supported by null ARID1A contrasts among SMARCA4-wildtype lines, R263 and R299. Second, KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency, represented by accepted reversal H17/R7 signed +0.796 (95% CI 0.776 to 0.816), validated by R13 +0.801 (95% CI 0.772 to 0.829), and repeated in high Cas9 R271 +0.800, lower Cas9 R279 +0.799, and many molecular strata. It is not modified by lineage, culture, screen quality, mutation burden, ploidy, aneuploidy, IFN, hypoxia, or MYC mRNA contrasts, for example R94, R98, R108, R119, R147, R170, R210, R257, R275, and R276. Third, MSI-high status is associated with much stronger WRN dependency: H8/R8 signed +0.790 (95% CI 0.760 to 0.819), validated by R52 +0.807 (95% CI 0.759 to 0.855). The association persists in high Cas9 R269 +0.776, lower Cas9 R280 +0.798, adenocarcinoma R24, TP53-null R44, TP53-lost R77, high and low screen-quality strata, growth-rate strata, ploidy and aneuploidy strata, serum strata, and BRCA2-null lines R264. Interactions with lineage, culture, growth rate, mutation burden, aneuploidy, IFN, and BRCA2 context are mostly not supported, for example R95, R99, R109, R144, R167, R190, R208, R211, R255, R261, and R265. Fourth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency: H14/R15 signed +0.267 (95% CI 0.215 to 0.319), validated by R26 +0.310 (95% CI 0.231 to 0.388). This direct PTEN-loss effect is reproduced in adenocarcinoma R27, TP53-null R28, TP53-lost R69, high and low Cas9 strata R270 and R281, IFN strata, low and high hypoxia strata R296 and R273, and media strata. Fifth, TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency: H12/R12 signed +0.396 (95% CI 0.325 to 0.467), validated by R65 +0.395 (95% CI 0.293 to 0.497). This is robust in high Cas9 R272 +0.390, lower Cas9 R282 +0.315, 10% serum R301 +0.443, and many molecular contexts. TP53 loss is not supported as a broad dependency marker for MDM2, STAT3, SMARCA2, WRN, or RPL11 in the tested contrasts, for example R6, R171, R184, R136, and R201. The only clear supported effect modification is interferon context for PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency. Direct PTEN-loss STAT3 associations are positive in moderate-to-high IFN strata, including IFN>=0.4 R287 +0.398, IFN>=0.5 R216 +0.428, IFN>=0.6 R230 +0.452, IFN>=0.7 R266 +0.447, IFN>=0.8 R242 +0.436, IFN>=0.9 R285 +0.371, and IFN>=1.0 R245 +0.342. Formal interactions are supported at IFN>=0.4 R288 +0.192, IFN>=0.5 R219 +0.221, IFN>=0.6 R231 +0.243, IFN>=0.7 R267 +0.222, IFN>=0.8 R243 +0.200, and in high-Cas9 subsets at IFN>=0.5 R284 +0.330 and IFN>=0.4 R295 +0.352. However, IFN>=0.9 R286 +0.118, IFN>=1.0 R246 +0.083, and low-tail R248 +0.127 are unsupported. Lower-Cas9 direct PTEN-loss STAT3 contrasts remain large, R290 +0.430 and R292 +0.430, but lower-Cas9 IFN interactions are not supported, R291 +0.079 and R293 +0.082. The IFN conclusion is therefore best interpreted as a rough dataset-specific context gradient, approximately moderate-to-high IFN amplification, not a precise mechanistic threshold at 0.4, 0.5, or 0.8. Low-IFN direct effects remain positive but smaller, for example IFN<=0.399 R294 +0.206, IFN<=0.499 R218 +0.207, IFN<=-0.5 R244 +0.138, and IFN<=-0.75 R247 +0.162. The IFN modification appears specific among tested core outcomes because IFN interactions are unsupported for SMARCA2 R254, WRN R255 and R261, USP7 R256, and NFE2L2 R257, and lower-Cas9 IFN interactions for USP7 R297 and SMARCA2 R298 are also null. Marker specificity is further supported by null research-marker contrasts R117, R154, R155, R167, and R168, and by null BRCA2 contrast among MSI-negative WRN lines R265. Important negative findings are broad and scientifically informative. KRAS mutation does not support the tested KRAS, RIT1, BRAF, or STAT3 dependency directions, for example R1, R16, R21, R122, R124, and R252. BRAF V600E does not support the tested BRAF, KRAS, EGFR, ERBB2, or RIT1 dependency directions, for example R2, R227, R228, R229, and R250. EGFR amplification does not support EGFR dependency in discovery R3 or validation R119, and does not support the tested ERBB2 direction R253. ERBB2 amplification does not support the tested ERBB2 or EGFR dependency directions, for example R4, R22, R123, R125, and R249. MYC DNA amplification is not meaningfully associated with the tested DHX9, POLR2A, RPL11, USP7, WRN, KIF18A, NFE2L2, or STAT3 dependency contrasts, for example R9, R10, R11, R51, R135, R137, R150, R152, and R173. Many conventional context interactions are null or unsupported, including lineage subtype R93, R94, R95, and R102, culture type R97, R98, R99, and R106, screen quality R107, R108, R109, and R110, PIK3CA R31, R33, and R79, KEAP1 or TP53 modification of other core effects R34, R46, R47, and R57, EMT R182 and R193, mutation-burden modification of core effects R144, R145, R146, R147, and R148, ploidy and aneuploidy interactions R206, R207, R208, R209, R210, and R211, growth-rate interactions R183, and hypoxia modification of PTEN-loss STAT3 R274. These nulls do not prove exact absence, but they sharply limit overinterpretation. Unresolved uncertainty remains substantial. The data are observational and cannot establish that SMARCA4 loss, KEAP1 loss, MSI-high status, PTEN loss, TP53 loss, or IFN context causes dependency-score differences. Correlated molecular features, screen batch, culture condition, ploidy, aneuploidy, and editing-quality metrics may partly confound context estimates. The IFN analysis uses overlapping dichotomized thresholds selected among many comparisons, so its threshold map is exploratory and approximate. Some direct and interaction estimates have small exposed cells, including lower-Cas9 IFN cells of 20 or 22. Several driver, PIK3CA, MYC, ERBB2/EGFR, and context claims remain deferred or unresolved, such as H27, H29, H30, H32, H33, H46, H47, H80, H81, H84, H92, H116, H130, H136, H137, H180, H185, and H194, and several interaction contrasts with wide intervals crossing zero remain not meaningful enough to accept. The most informative next analysis, if the controller can move beyond repeated Welch threshold tests, would be a continuous or spline model for dependency_STAT3 with PTEN-loss exposure and IFN_gamma_signature, including Cas9_activity_score and relevant batch, culture, screen-quality, ploidy, and mutation-burden covariates, with a formal interaction test and residual diagnostics. Within the current Welch framework, finer non-overlapping IFN bins and explicit Cas9-stratified comparisons would be the next-best same-dataset robustness step, but independent validation capacity is exhausted and causal or generalizable inference remains unsupported.

results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.

expectation

plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: No assessments are due and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so this final exploration registers new discovery comparisons only. The main objective now is to sharpen the two most informative unresolved questions from the accumulated evidence: (1) whether the accepted PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency association and its approximate interferon gradient behave sensibly in non-overlapping context bins and editing-quality strata, and (2) whether the five core marker-dependency associations persist in the genome-stability-relevant low-ploidy complement rather than only the already-tested high-ploidy stratum. The proposed PTEN-loss STAT3 analyses define three complementary direct-effect regions: IFN in [0.4,0.8), IFN in [-0.75,0.4), and the lower-IFN complement of the accepted lower/higher Cas9 high-IFN contrasts. They also add a direct low-ploidy PTEN-loss test, a low-ploidy IFN interaction test, and a common 10% serum plus IFN>=0.5 direct test. These comparisons are intended to distinguish a broad context gradient from an artifact of overlapping threshold cuts and to test whether interferon modification persists when both IFN and editing quality or genome instability are jointly bounded. For each signed comparison, acceptance will require the 95% interval to exclude zero and the signed magnitude to be scientifically meaningful, using the practical 0.10 dependency-score-unit benchmark maintained throughout this run. The low-ploidy core marker comparisons test SMARCA4 loss on SMARCA2, KEAP1 loss on NFE2L2, MSI-high on WRN, TP53 loss on USP7, and PTEN loss on STAT3 in a stratum with more near-diploid genome content; strong positive signed effects would strengthen dataset-specific robustness, while null effects would limit claims that the associations hold across all genome-instability contexts. The ARID1A-loss control among SMARCA4-wildtype low-ploidy lines tests marker specificity in a cleaner SMARCA4-complement context; prior ARID1A nulls make a meaningful association unlikely, but this remains a useful final specificity check. All conclusions from these analyses will remain associations in the supplied lung-derived dataset only, not causal effects and not claims of generalizability to other screens or populations.
